name: House DFL
subject: A Statement from Sophie and Colin Hortman
disclaimer_text: paid for by the
body:
Hello all,
Sophie and Colin Hortman released the following statement on behalf of the Hortman family. We wanted to make sure you saw it:
“We are devastated and heartbroken at the loss of our parents, Melissa and Mark. They were the bright lights at the center of our lives, and we can’t believe they are gone. Their love for us was boundless. We miss them so much.
“We want everyone to know that we are both safe and with loved ones. We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support we have received, and we appreciate your respect for our family’s privacy as we grieve.
“Our family would like to thank law enforcement for their swift action that saved others and for the coordination across communities that led to the arrest of the man who murdered our parents. We especially would like to thank the officers who were first on the scene to our parents’ home and their heroic attempts to rescue our mom and dad.
“Our parents touched so many lives, and they leave behind an incredible legacy of dedication to their community that will live on in us, their friends, their colleagues and co-workers, and every single person who knew and loved them.
“If you would like to honor the memory of Mark and Melissa, please consider the following:
* Plant a tree.
* Visit a local park and make use of their amenities, especially a bike trail.
* Pet a dog. A golden retriever is ideal, but any will do.
* Tell your loved ones a cheesy dad joke and laugh about it.
* Bake something — bread for Mark or a cake for Melissa, and share it with someone.
* Try a new hobby and enjoy learning something.
* Stand up for what you believe in, especially if that thing is justice and peace.
“Hope and resilience are the enemy of fear. Our parents lived their lives with immense dedication to their fellow humans. This tragedy must become a moment for us to come together. Hold your loved ones a little closer. Love your neighbors. Treat each other with kindness and respect. The best way to honor our parents' memory is to do something, whether big or small, to make our community just a little better for someone else.”
Thank you for taking the time to read this email. We’ll get through this together.
House DFL
Prepared and paid for by the
DFL House Caucus
255 East Plato Blvd
Saint Paul MN 55107

name: Shelby Wiltz (via Democrats.org)
subject: Introducing myself 👋
body:
---
Hi Derek, I’m Shelby Wiltz, the new Political Director at the DNC. I’ve spent most of my career working to elect Democrats outside of the beltway — from Virginia to Iowa to Nevada — and right now, it’s more crucial than ever that we elect Democrats up and down the ballot who will act as a check against Trump and his extremist Republican allies. Now, as the DNC’s Political Director, I am laser-focused on using my experience to help us win in 2025, 2026, and beyond. That means building relationships and implementing new strategies so we can compete and organize everywhere. As Chair Ken Martin says, we need to get the DNC out of D.C., which means meeting voters where they are — in rural communities, red districts, and every corner of the country. Building those relationships _now_ will be crucial in our efforts to elect Democrats across the country. **But we can’t do this work without you.** That’s why I’m hoping you make a donation to the DNC today. $3 — that’s the ask. $3 to build lasting infrastructure in _every_ state, and make sure Democrats have the tools to compete everywhere. $3 to support the organizers who are building year-round relationships with voters in places Democrats can’t afford to overlook. $3 to elect Democrats up and down the ballot — in state legislatures, governors’ races, Senate contests, and the presidency — and stop Trump and Republicans from dismantling our democracy. If you believe in this work — if you believe in the power of a Party that organizes early, everywhere, and for everyone — I hope you’ll chip in. [**Can you please contribute $3 (or whatever you can afford) to the DNC today?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-june-2025?refcode=em_20250624_3803_fr&amount=3&refcode2=3803_22930333_XyNYA8&akid=3803%2E22930333%2EXyNYA8) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly:_ | | | **[CONTRIBUTE $3](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-june-2025?express_lane=true&amount=3&refcode=em_20250624_3803_fr&refcode2=3803_22930333_XyNYA8&akid=3803%2E22930333%2EXyNYA8)**

**Mitch McConnell Says People Worried About Medicaid Cuts Will 'Get Over It'
\- _Newsweek_** Peter,

Medicaid covers one third of Kentuckians, half of Kentucky kids, and 70% of the long term care costs our seniors rely on. The bill that Republicans are negotiating in the Senate will gut this coverage and threaten rural healthcare all over the country.

And what does Kentucky Senator Mitch McConnell, in a closed-door meeting with other Republican senators, have to say about this?

**“I know a lot of us are hearing from people back home about Medicaid. But they’ll get over it.”**

Folks, 16 million Americans are going to lose their healthcare if this bill becomes law. What McConnell said is callous and cruel.

This is not what leadership looks like. As I’ve said many times, our elected leaders should make decisions with the best interests of their people in mind.

I’m fighting for better leadership here in Kentucky and across the country, because we can’t allow people in Washington to keep passing laws that hurt people. clean_body: Mitch McConnell doesn’t care. Mitch McConnell Says People Worried About Medicaid Cuts Will 'Get Over It' \- Newsweek Peter, Medicaid covers one third of Kentuckians, half of Kentucky kids, and 70% of the long term care costs our seniors rely on. The bill that Republicans are negotiating in the Senate will gut this coverage and threaten rural healthcare all over the country. And what does Kentucky Senator Mitch McConnell, in a closed-door meeting with other Republican senators, have to say about this? “I know a lot of us are hearing from people back home about Medicaid. But they’ll get over it.” Folks, 16 million Americans are going to lose their healthcare if this bill becomes law. What McConnell said is callous and cruel. This is not what leadership looks like. As I’ve said many times, our elected leaders should make decisions with the best interests of their people in mind. I’m fighting for better leadership here in Kentucky and across the country, because we can’t allow people in Washington to keep passing laws that hurt people. subject: Why I’ll never stop fighting

body:
The Supreme Court’s decision has set us back a generation in the fight for women’s reproductive freedom.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110187516/553590119/2145345036?refcode=BLU_EM_GOOD_2025-06-24_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTMwMjAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiODI1YTFkODctNjI1MS1mMDExLThmN2MtNjA0NWJkZmU4ZTljIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=uFPlCxQP67JAjaqqPkcWZqm4Hg7Fam9Y1Je3QR_4j_s=)
---
| Peter,

Three years ago today, the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , undoing nearly 50 years of precedent and ending constitutional protections for women who need access to reproductive health care across New Hampshire and the nation.

The Supreme Court’s decision has set us back generations in the fight for women’s reproductive freedom. It has emboldened extremists across America — including here in New Hampshire — to further restrict access to life-saving reproductive health care. They are pursuing an extreme agenda to further restrict access to abortion, IVF, and even contraception nationwide.

When I was almost 20 weeks pregnant, we got the devastating news that we had lost our son.

| | **Register now for the 2025 WAGOP Action Conference
Sept. 5-7th!**
**Bellevue** —Join us for the third annual [WAGOP Action Conference](https://wsrp.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be1a8605f1118163852707f35&id=6b35024bcd&e=6a281f566d) set for **Sept. 5th -7 th in Yakima**. We have a great program lined up this year with panels ranging from how to talk to voters and recruit activists to interacting with the government in impactful ways. You are bound to learn something new this year! We will be hosting the panels and a banquet with great speakers and organizations on Saturday, with a final panel Sunday morning featuring WAGOP, HROC, and SRCC leaders - but join us early on Friday night at our Welcome Reception for more fun and socializing with fellow Republicans! **When** : September 5th – 7th **Where:** Yakima Convention & Event Center
10 North 8th Street
Yakima, WA 98901

**What:** Trainings, social events, networking, and great speakers!

**Why:** To empower grassroots activism ahead of the 2025 and 2026 elections--in hopes of turning WA RED!

Don’t delay. Please register now for the 2025 WAGOP Action Conference.

We hope to see you there!

Team WAGOP

But does imposing higher tax rates on wealthy Americans actually increase the amount of revenue coming into the federal government? | | | Donald Trump wants a Nobel Peace Prize, and his sycophantic followers are pushing hard for him to get it. [**Tell the Nobel Committee HELL NO. **](https://default.salsalabs.org/T5f6b5b2a-091f-4381-9a40-c00a2a0c8aad/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) Trump doesn't deserve a Nobel Prize for his work on the Iran crisis. He doesn't even merit a participation trophy. Trump was the one who tore up the earlier agreement, helping cause this crisis in the first place. And there are a whole host of other ways and other places he has helped stir up violence and subvert peace over the years. But his followers are already putting pressure on the Nobel judges, and will no doubt use threats of violence to try to get their way (which is ironic, but they're too dumb to realize that). Everyone involved in the award process needs to hear from us as well, and we need to urge them to resist the Trump lunatics, and give the prize to someone more deserving (basically, any other human). ## Trump Brokers Truce in Israel-Iran Fight
President Trump has [reinstated a ceasefire between Israel and Iran](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQxvGngc0RPjhsDwxdvKVrR4uYI1yFTYRJorx9lQ59gc6f9Jd-39d5OXvOvF8__UauxbLs9DwytUZ1WckfFLlSKjnwfl3vZSu5HLSAAuyU7QCX4Dm_FiODi0RAWpLrB1SjwQmNTG4weujBw0WNasQLTiOi0RZjWEldopbs3jVlAXulEPXJjmHywVgKfY9RB2EUBW6lnr4L7y1RzK_yoHpayyazS63dDqE_BMwC5pYocc7vTcCcykZvkIAZtcWhn7pW79ut46N6yh1Xv3d_TAGzrC7cnpwzH3YQRl03z78x2f71zsPBTwAAAP__mJ14TA) after both sides briefly resumed attacks, drawing a sharp rebuke from the president. _“They’ve been fighting so long and so hard they don’t know what the f--- they’re doing,”_ [Trump told reporters](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAQQL8Gu9kgCmpBcY3dXnulmZVBuUUwwK7x7y_uL1w3mZe8zLyf-3RH511YvnEjXWycAh3ZUymUppkwk3WJ1uiNC8v8ilv0MdMkuJDAFQg5GXT-nNrKaEskqKlI153kfSsH2VarblSn6oHEoPBhGq5mblXf9YSIQ61EXzl92bgSsuZcyuamejOgaRWZupa2MazlZFyJ6fYbXSgrWX_GN6XbHLfK67WUPbPmi4mRiTGce8zlQkyMl5iJkatrbpkYXxmu_5gYS3ptOzw8bpTBJQyAwYDLCcmDjQkeifDpwgKfCnBlgIxnhrLSCSaGAs8QDzhWLNcOLDw_LBGY6MLCxFglbfbDee-y6ljLlw2d_5xd_tX6rcVfAAAA__8KzpOr) before heading to a NATO summit. After a tense call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Trump said Israel agreed to call off further strikes. Trump said the truce was “very much in effect” and expressed optimism it would hold “for a long time.” A GOP congressman nominated Trump [for the Nobel Peace Prize](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1upDAURp8GOiPjHwYXLrahm223RAZfD3d1sZHtGTJ5-ogUeYHUn3T0nfPvPt8dEsbHX7eDrSHNEc5CUCvkeQVXIGCGLZHH-FifaU-UCsyCC834wISevUN6z6r1NgAIkC3Y_qb5qLTRqt1sr0XvjOa9GY0OehQ3ucIyGqWWIM0iW7QXjQ9C95xrLbth9MZ5NYDvex2kbxQHjzXl7n_CWDcI9E4vyN2a9pbsVutRGvmnEVMjpvM8u5A-Lotrb8R0JMKKa2nEVPNzP1hMO0ZXwbOYFiB2gFuBHRk_gV1chtlFhiU7IPbTgHlw1GbrjxOJsAy3RvHH7pC-f9RfxXtZ8RUAAP__POSF-Q) for the ceasefire.
## Mamdani Beats Cuomo in NYC Primary
Democratic socialist candidate [Zohran Mamdani won ](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAMhp8mbKmCIdAOGW5h6603Ijdxik8JQUloxduf6CvcZEuf9cn__3Of78iB1-c3RjLVp3mldwlUK-XZEhbynGlJwfH6tHuKKaRCMyjQUg0S9OyQwzH3jTOeCKhryLSjVtde33TfLGawOJKDhx71FTsFhM5p8jccrfLwUA2b06YG0K1SWneX4epu6PqBXNtq3znRK3JcU778Jl7rQj4c6UX5YlNsgllq3YrovgRMAqb12FKpJxIwnWIBkxrOvRcw7UWe-T53VkY8UsYgt8wR8yEpkK2cVhn4RXLfHFYqMlPZQz0nfmiRPqcoM1oqEm1Opci6kLRcDwFTk43b3hwCl2EUvXpG5PB5tf6r35eBvwAAAP__EjCRdQ)the first round of the Democratic primary for New York City mayor Tuesday by a surprisingly large margin over former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo.

Cuomo called Assemblyman Zohran Mamdani to congratulate him on the victory, then said his campaign was "going to take a look and make some decisions." The race will be officially [decided by ranked choice voting](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSrCAURL9GMyxEQCcgeInZvHRD6w5cxrsLYgEzln-_5fzCxqe6q09_3Zc7UKDt-R8imurTsuFRAtaKebEIBT1lXFNwtD3tK8UUUsFFcKEY10yoxQGFc5GtMx5R4NCi6UfFJ6luSrarGT0IOQ3SKzl6GP2k_diL6SG4muChdEvmauNaqJ5zpYZOT-4GTmp0fa_84BrJ0VFNuftOtNUVfTjTG3NnU2yDWWvdSzP8a8TciPk4js4-ymVx8UbMGx5nyj-NmAO9kb12BxXLBU7LIpwpF5bBInMYk81QybI9U4R8so8nBrSV0sYylleoV7TNxu0HhUBFj43kzwgUPnvqn058G_EbAAD__1xEiBk) since no candidate received 50% in the first round.

Mamdani, a 33-year-old Democratic socialist, held 43.5% of the vote to Cuomo's 36.3% with 80% of the votes counted by late Tuesday night.
## 60s Pop Star Bobby Sherman Dies at 81
Bobby Sherman, 1960s pop sensation and star of ABC-TV's _Here Come the Brides_ , [died at age 81](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZEbGxsAEDi4hm0svRA3dHvtk6JHtHcTfr2b2EzapqFSq9_7dlzvEFI_HX9jJVc_LQWdJVCvlZSMo5GOmwAnj8di-eOfEhRattJVqkNouCDFdS9-g80SaTEOuG62aenuzfROc8h2MaiMPnrwBMGDHyY4TIIJHsE107zU1aNspZa1phwlvgP1A2HXWGxS9IoyVc_uf41ED-XTxi3K78d4kF2p9FmH-CD0LPZ_n2QZO6TqZMdOTc_1pCj3X1yfkG1HoeeV1vWQJlHc4JBKgrESHjMhJBsokN95J1kByzRGpyE6bQd8mbazQc5MdPs-YUizDKHr12CGmz6f6K5Evp78DAAD__70UiWI) after a battle with cancer. Sherman rose to fame on ABC’s _Shindig!_ and scored several chart-topping hits, including _Little Woman_ and _Julie, Do Ya Love Me_. [Watch a music video here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1ugzAUxfGnsbcg46-QwUOlKlsytepoGfsa38rgCAyUt6_oK3Q9R_oN_6-HfTjMOA1PN4KpsdgJ9iVDrTBbD26BiDOkkgNOg1_LWHJZwHLG1YXpC1c2OMyHlTSYCMBBUDDtVbFOqpuSNBlgwV29Ztr1Xeid86LTrfDiprnUSgBFc2pMc9UyppRodBduLkgNoW1VFIFIBgFrmZvvglNNEPNRNpgbX0aaTar1tRDxRvid8Pu-781R1rr2cP7n4qpPRNw3It7VM316_hPhQ9LZhNeOOeOir0SyYXSY_8j6rw6b4b8BAAD__2C-cU4). ## Officers Injured, Suspect Killed in Texas Tech Shooting
Two Texas Tech police officers were [shot early Tuesday morning](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu6yAQRVeDOyyYgMEFxW_c5bevtBwYBxRiLDOJk90_2Vt43UgjnXvP_bmO1ynltNz_T0909JnLuOBeMxLhNhJ-pkroY42lUFrusbwqlaWOIEBz0XHQY5hS_o6qCe4mQi8bdNJoYVUP1jbRKUTsjTAAZpKq742VHrT11uh5CuLSJHfARAdaSiFBttZoo252tqCVCL1nSmBIVLaWIp6V5vwtb9xaX55NdpForezyj8HAYNj3vX34WzieDIaDzWAQ3XErBoPkK261LPyRcsbAT7XyIr4nivzE80OZryUnjwyGZnNh3VPOqXaGKXF_Timf2fS3xd4OfgMAAP___LF-vA) while investigating a suspicious vehicle in a campus parking lot. The officers sustained non-life-threatening injuries, and the suspect was killed when the officers returned fire. Officials [have not provided the names](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O6yAUhVdjd1hwAwYXFK9Jl9dOaWG4DijEROZOSHY_cqRZwfTn7ztfl_niUk7b9b-7o6XXWuYNW81IhPtM-HKV0McaS6G0XWP5rlS2OgMHxfjIQM3BpfyeZR_swsMkerRCK27kBMb00epRjw60M9ovfAnL6paTdgjeSx_EiffJHmF8BCUEFyAGo5WWi1kNKMnD5DvJMSQq-0ARP5PW_C5P3Adf7n22kehRu9O_Ds4dnFtrw4HQEG-HoIPzx8MODvYLwlp0xBqy21YaA26mSYl-t-HRUs6pjrqT_Hp3KX9K6G_XPC38BAAA__9bA3m6) of the suspect or the officers who were shot. One of the officers was released from the hospital, while the other is still receiving treatment. Around 12:45 a.m., the two officers approached the vehicle, which had its doors open, in the parking lot on the north side of Jones AT&T Stadium. A person made "some furtive gestures around the vehicle” before [pulling out a gun](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OwyAQhU-DO1vDBGIoKLZxl223RISfgERMZGbj5PYr5wrbTTHv0_vez8VeXKllvX27ezT0Ss2uce81EsXNUny5TtHnnlujst5y--3U1m4RUI5wHlHa4Ep9WzEEc4Wg-RANnyUooVGpIRvlPMoEXjuveDgFcQoQZu6DV9pr4EMxBwzOKDkHjnxSs5zFVSWFUkDQngmIoVDbJsrxUynVd3vGbfLtPlSTiR6dnb4YLgyXfd-n1F7i0DgeGC7HyXD5RMdDZ2wpFR-3PvbcaNhMeOyl1tLPMxNwu7tSP2z63yJPg38BAAD__wtvdvA) and firing on the officers. The chief of the Texas Tech Police Department said the suspect is not affiliated with the university. The Lubbock Metropolitan Special Crimes Unit is [investigating the shooting](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGO5CAQRL8GZ4wAw9gOHJx0IttLL7QAt8e9i8GC9njn708e6b5gsw66u15V_f2YPhxGTI8_boORvpc8JThrBCIoE8G3qwRhrWvOhOmx5qNSTnVSQhku7lyZaXYYX5Nu5tGLeZANjLIzoteD6vtmHXVYjDFOdIOEQXcwtz5IEF4GN3jthwbH65m4KyOlkEre-s502vdLr4wW8xCYFjAj5XKjFd5IS3zlJ5RbyFsTx5Vor6z9xZRlyp7neYuH9zl85RQxwbXFlK2Uy4spe9ljyoaCGzBlL22mrLhfs2bKSr5DqTnxL4wRZu4WgsL_B8Ad8TcCv2LhR8InlIr04sFt-1H5niMG4HlZMECpHNPnUa5DxT-PBPyt0eu2FXcjhegu6NaSL7Cw9ve6N2Wc9xNjxHrvmBaPzWF8G6Wf1fMc1b8AAAD__z5opKs).
## Special Session Agenda
In addition to vetoing legislation to ban THC-infused hemp products, Gov. Greg Abbott [vetoed over two dozen other bills](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2yqyAUhZ8GOx3YAcSC4jZ2ue0pGQybwAyRjOzE5O3P6Cucfv18a_1c3dXnktf7f_9AS59Y3Yp7K0iEmyP8-EZ4Sy3VSnm9p_pqVNfmgIPque5BueBz-TrZBbvwMIkOrRgVN3ICY7pktRDR6CmGqIICqUceAnIdJykvaLTssj3CuAYlBBcgBjOqUS4mGlCSh-nGJMeQqW4DJTyRYvnWN27DrT66YhPRs7HLPwYzg3nf9yHWz-hfjfJ6SBjMxyYG82nu30i198tSifoll9L6A6DbbHjuuZTc9Mgkvz98LmcD_e2Xt4XfAAAA___-33e7) late Sunday evening before calling a special session to revisit several issues addressed in those bills. In addition to tackling THC regulation, Abbott has also tasked lawmakers with [addressing](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SgyAURp9GOx24okJBsY1dtt3SQbgEZlCycBOTt99JXmH78_3M-bmsFxNTPK7fZkdNT5_XA8-akAjLSvg0ldCGGnKmeFxDvlfKR12BwdixqYNxdSam1ypapzfmFG9R83lkUiiQsg16sFLwzYOQyohhUJsYhfRgmRgmM4Fro36XsQlGzhkH3st5nMUmvYRRMKdsIxi6SLn0FPBzyadXfmDpbd7bpAPRrTbDVwNLA8t5nm_O4kFY6u_dFHxzDSyfaAOLKRRtwlX5CSdvbWf9LDvhnOkU81sHTikOm5UDc32gPbVFu9sZU4p1mhvBrruJ6TNO_1P20PAXAAD__zUjf48) judicial procedures, the prosecution of human trafficking and prostitution, the regulation of cement kilns, home title theft, and fees associated with new housing developments. Among the bills Abbott vetoed and [did not add to the special session agenda](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2y3CAMhZ8Gd-xg2finoEjj7qZN6cEgsCas2QHFvvv2Ge_kDdKpkD595_z6Wr8sJTriT_tEw98hrwdeNSEzlpXx21ZGt9c9Z6Yj7vlP5XzUFRRoqQYJevWW0nvtG2825ee2QdOOWk39DNPU7GbbghsH8FrZFoagPGjnOt-pPoR5At-QuWFqAN22qoX2MY167LcpTKB75WcneoWeOJcH7_hRCumdTywPl59NMjvzq4ruh4BFwHJd18Mlcr_hn-y9JWC5YwlYPvcClvungEUN99wJWGI-ZSwYpd22zCxz8ViqrC90ZJNMGKkmy3SirFgr5UPawFjkiZzpiBIGuVFKN7wpxr8uSonqMIpexael9LHl_-v4NPA3AAD__zBckig) was one that would have ensured that a defendant is not imprisoned before trial for longer than the punishment if convicted, and another allowing teachers to serve on property appraisal review boards. Abbott also used his line-item veto to cancel $60 million in spending from the state budget, which would have unlocked at least $400 million in federal funding to [provide summer lunches for children](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOpCAYhJ8Gb3TwB5E-eNik4232ukcD8otkUDrw2_a8_cZ-hblVqpIvVfXva_qyMcU9_LUbDvRe8rTjWRMSYZkI37YSzmtdc6a4hzUflfJeJxDQcaE5dJO3Mf1MqvGDE_7eNji0fSeMuoMxzTpIqxYjlQOtnNTYm-6uepRGGg3WKNfE4YIJDV3bihbam-m7XjmzGOiU8PeZKYE-Ui43WvFTaUk_-YXlNuetScNK9KxM_mEwMhjP87x9n_S-QgbjxWYwCn1pyWAM-cVDwcCtc5mIv5AyVr4cu4974At6LDbxemwbFp6OfV75s-RQ7IVjcjxom2o-yoxMPsi6nJNloC97Qx-PjclHLsHucZ5TnL8rA02u4MLkY302ZfDPM6YUq-6ZEmGzMX2G0O_ufw3wPwAA__-D65rN) in low-income families.
## Heavy Rains Reveal Ancient Fossil
A paleontologist from Dallas recently discovered the [fossilized skull of an ancient amphibian](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOqzAQRb8GOpA92GAKF69Jl9duiYht4tFOMLInIfn7FWj_YLujGencq_t1na4zEq73__MjWH4vaVrDXigwhzxxeM-Fg4slpsS43mN6Fk5rmUCAbkTfgJ78jPSZVO3tTfhR1sHKQQujRjCmjlaJ4BeQvTQwQDd0frwJ5zqhvVSyM2ON9pCJHrSUQoJszaAHdTOLAa2EH111KJBTbjmGs9JCn_QKuXXpUZONzFupun8VXCq47PveupjTenwruBAu4Tgj-V-cM6Ojg05Zs6RSkJry_SRqQHRmVMa0W9zqbP22IxGWfqiUuD9mpDOU_zbVy8JPAAAA__8tnn0h) at the Permian Quarry in Archer County after heavy rains washed away sediment covering the remains. Andre LuJan, the director of the Texas Through Time Fossil Museum in Hillsboro, [identified the skull](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOqzAQheGnMV2QPdcGU7iIckW1SbslGvAAlgyO7NmQvP0qeYXtjz4d_d_X4Yohhn254UaOn3MadjpKJGbKA9MTC9O0ljUlDvuypp_CaS8DSDAn2ZzADB5DfA268m6UvlMVOdUaaXUH1larmxVQN9JoJ8JJe2vQeNv5Bq1sO4lYBffGZANGKalA1bY1rR7tbMFo6btJaEk-cMo1r_S5NMdXelCup7RV0a3M9yL-nQX0AvrjOOqwF8Yl4_ZeCOgzURTQ__-6tLidrufLTUBfZefvR4gxlKYVWi4bhvgh-W8hHg5-AwAA__-ZLHIy) as that of _Eryops megacephalus_ , an extinct amphibian predator with a large, flat head. Its wide jaws suggest it wasn’t able to chew and instead swallowed prey by tossing its head back, similar to alligators and crocodiles. "_This is an exciting discovery_ ," said LuJan. "_It's a well-known animal and not considered rare, but this discovery is significant because even though it's damaged, it is nearly complete_.” Once the specimen is extracted, LuJan will take it to the museum for cleaning and restoration, a process that could take up to a year. I'm a little unsure about opening up to you this way.

The deck is stacked against us, my back is against the wall, and your response to this message will decide everything.

My name is Pat Harrigan. You don't know me, but I'm a Green Beret veteran from North Carolina. I graduated from West Point, and I served 18 months in combat.

After that, my wife and I started a firearm parts company from our double-wide trailer - and grew it to become a successful, job-creating business. And most important of all, I'm the dad of two beautiful girls.

Look - I won't give you empty promises & fancy slogans. That's not me.

Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. name: All On The Line
subject: The details, the aftermath, and where we’re at now:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE NATIONAL REDISTRICTING ACTION FUND
body:
It’s been 12 years since the Shelby County decision rolled back VRA protections. Here’s where we’re at now:
|
---

Peter,
Today marks the 12-year anniversary of the Supreme Court’s disastrous _Shelby County_ decision.
_**The details:**_ The decision nullified Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act, effectively gutting preclearance — a safeguard that had been in place since 1965 to prevent states from implementing discriminatory barriers. States saw this move as an open invitation for states to make voting hard for people of color, and for extremists to manipulate maps. The VRA’s preclearance provision mandated that jurisdictions with a record of voter discrimination were obligated to get federal approval before making any changes to their election law, including redistricting plans.
**_The aftermath:_** States immediately began to engage in efforts to restrict access to the ballot. body:
I’ll always put New Hampshire first.

I’m Congressman Chris Pappas, and Elissa Slotkin said I could reach out with some big news:
**I’m officially running to be New Hampshire’s next U.S. Senator, and I have the endorsement of Senator Elissa Slotkin.** I’m going to share more about why I’m in this race, but if you’re already on board, [**split a contribution to my campaign and Elissa Slotkin today.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-pappas-split._m_z_j&refcode=em250625-1-&refcode2=slotkin-ms-cp-em-slotkin&t=2&akid=2295%2E135344%2EwNsP01)
I’m running for Senate because at this pivotal moment, our economy, our democracy, and our way of life are on the line. New Hampshire deserves a Senator who is grounded in the people, places, and values of this state – and one who is ready to lead on day one.
Our country is at a crossroads, and the decisions we make now will have generational impacts. You can count on me to continue taking on big fights and confronting the Trump Administration, self-dealing billionaires, and extreme politicians who are threatening our future and our ability to get things done for New Hampshire.
**[**Can I count on you to become a Founding Donor to my campaign with a $5 contribution, split between my campaign and Elissa Slotkin right now? We can’t win this race without major grassroots support.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-pappas-split._m_z_j&refcode=em250625-1-&refcode2=slotkin-ms-cp-em-slotkin&t=3&akid=2295%2E135344%2EwNsP01)
**These fights are deeply personal to me.** My family immigrated from Greece and opened a restaurant in Manchester 108 years ago, a small business that remains at the heart of the community today. Running that small business showed me the power of hard work and serving others, but the opportunity that my ancestors and so many others like them sought has never been further away – and the Trump Administration is too busy cutting deals for their billionaire buddies to give a damn.
I’m also openly gay and happily married to my husband, Vann. With the current wave of hateful policies leveled at the LGBTQ+ community, I know how important representation is at this moment. **If elected, I’d be the first openly gay male U.S. Senator in history** – a badge of honor I’d wear proudly as I advocate for full equality.
I am the proud product of public education, and I come from a family of business owners _(my grandfather invented the chicken tender at the restaurant – seriously!)_. I understand firsthand the need to support neighborhood schools and small businesses in our community. **These are the lifeblood of our economy and the pillars of opportunity for everyone.**
My life experiences are what led me to successfully run for four terms in Congress and win in one of the “swingiest” districts in the nation. Before I won my election in 2018, no one had managed to hold the seat for more than one term for more than a decade. I’m no stranger to tough electoral fights.**Now I’m ready to take on the fight to keep New Hampshire’s Senate seat blue.**
We can’t afford to sit on the sidelines of the big fights ahead – not with so much at stake, from the rising costs debilitating working families to the threats to the future of our democracy. We’ve taken on big fights together in Congress. Now it’s time to win this critical Senate seat so we can keep standing up to the Trump Administration and the self-dealing billionaires threatening our future. Can I count on you to join the fight?
**[**If you’re with me, let’s make a powerful statement together and prove that we’re ready to win this race. Become a Founding Donor with a $5 donation to my campaign and Elissa Slotkin now.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-pappas-split._m_z_j&refcode=em250625-1-&refcode2=slotkin-ms-cp-em-slotkin&t=4&akid=2295%2E135344%2EwNsP01)
Thank you again to Elissa Slotkin for letting me reach out today and for endorsing my campaign.
With gratitude,
Chris

East Lansing, MI 48826

# NATO praises Trump for Iran-Israel peace deal and making Europe pay their fair share
President Donald Trump **[received praise from NATO leaders](https://substack.com/redirect/8d1c4b31-46f1-4bdc-a4bc-f4350ab8db70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Tuesday for brokering the Iran-Israel ceasefire and pressuring Europe into a new 5% defense spending target, though he maintained ambiguity about U.S. commitment to the alliance's mutual defense obligations during the second day of the summit.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8d1c4b31-46f1-4bdc-a4bc-f4350ab8db70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Trump received praise for bringing peace** \- NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte congratulated Trump via text for his "decisive action on Iran" and for "making Europe pay in a big way" through a new 5% defense spending target that represents a significant increase from the previous 2% goal.
* **NATO members agreed to boost defense spending to 5% of GDP, with most of the burden falling on European allies** \- The new target breaks down into 3.5% for core defense spending and 1.5% for related infrastructure like cyberwarfare, though Trump said the U.S. doesn't need to reach the full threshold since it already spends about 3.4% on defense.
* **Trump maintained his cordial but ambiguous stance on NATO's mutual defense commitments** \- While offering a surprisingly friendly tone toward the alliance he has long criticized, Trump cast doubt on whether the U.S. would honor Article 5's mutual defense clause, saying "it depends on your definition" and that there are "numerous definitions" of the commitment.
* **The summit highlighted NATO's focus on countering Russian military production despite economic disadvantages** \- Rutte emphasized that it's "unthinkable that Russia, with an economy 25 times smaller than NATO's, should be able to outproduce and outgun us," urging European allies to strengthen defenses and increase military production on both sides of the Atlantic.

# Socialist beats Cuomo in NYC mayoral primary
Socialist assemblyman Zohran Mamdani **[defeated former three-term Gov. Andrew Cuomo 43% to 36%](https://substack.com/redirect/efe7f6da-de24-447b-9bab-f13430eb39ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in Tuesday's Democratic mayoral primary, a stunning upset that political analysts called a "political earthquake" signaling the party's leftward shift as younger, progressive voters reshape New York City politics.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/da9fa447-4730-46d0-9fe3-fe6474629be6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Mamdani's defeat of Andrew Cuomo signals a major leftward shift in Democratic politics** \- The 33-year-old socialist assemblyman decisively beat the former governor, creating a moment for progressives and younger voters to reshape the Democratic Party similar to AOC's 2018 upset victory over Joe Crowley.
* **Socialism and economic populism resonated with young and working class voters despite establishment opposition** \- Mamdani's proposals to tax the rich and provide free services like bus fares connected with young voters and working class people, even as he was outspent by Cuomo's $25 million Super PAC and faced opposition from most major labor unions who backed the former governor.
* **The victory creates challenges for Democratic establishment figures and may embolden other socialist challengers** \- Party leaders like Governor Kathy Hochul and Senator Chuck Schumer must decide whether to endorse Mamdani, while his win could inspire other democratic socialists to challenge incumbent Democrats in Congress, though his leftist positions on public safety and Israel may hurt him in the general election against Mayor Eric Adams and Republican Curtis Sliwa.
* **Strong opponent to Israel** \- Mamdani has expressed strong criticism towards Israel and is **[reportedly linked to anti-Israel activist groups](https://substack.com/redirect/b8bf682d-afe3-485b-999a-c4207f31b9f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in New York.

# Joe Rogan puts Bernie Sanders in his place for criticizing Elon Musk helping Trump
Sen. Bernie Sanders criticized Elon Musk's $270 million donation to Donald Trump's campaign during a Tuesday appearance on "The Joe Rogan Experience," but the podcast host quickly countered by noting Kamala Harris raised $1.5 billion in her losing presidential bid, highlighting how both parties rely on massive donor contributions.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5054ff80-208d-4329-bbec-63a8ef914028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Sanders criticized Elon Musk's $270 million donation to Trump while condemning the Citizens United decision** \- The Vermont senator called the Supreme Court ruling "maybe the worst decision" ever made and argued it gives billionaires a "constitutional right" to influence elections through massive spending, citing Musk's contributions as an example of the problem.
* **Rogan countered by highlighting Kamala Harris's $1.5 billion campaign spending** \- When Sanders attacked Musk's donations, Rogan pointed out that the Harris campaign raised and spent $1.5 billion in just 15 weeks and still ended up $20 million in debt, pointing out that both sides benefit from big money in politics.
* **Sanders acknowledged that both parties rely on billionaire donors despite his criticism** \- The self-described democratic socialist admitted he doesn't limit his criticism to Republicans, saying "it wasn't just Musk and the Republicans putting a lot of money into Trump, it was Democratic billionaires putting money into Kamala and other candidates as well."

If you want to learn more about , go ahead read this that just went up. It's filled with some valuable information about what's in store for America, and what we could potentially be up against. Yours Truly, SEAN HANNITY | | ---|---|--- NATO praises Trump for Iran-Israel peace deal and making Europe pay their fair share President Donald Trump Tuesday for brokering the Iran-Israel ceasefire and pressuring Europe into a new 5% defense spending target, though he maintained ambiguity about U.S. commitment to the alliance's mutual defense obligations during the second day of the summit. | | ---|---|--- Trump received praise for bringing peace \- NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte congratulated Trump via text for his "decisive action on Iran" and for "making Europe pay in a big way" through a new 5% defense spending target that represents a significant increase from the previous 2% goal. NATO members agreed to boost defense spending to 5% of GDP, with most of the burden falling on European allies \- The new target breaks down into 3.5% for core defense spending and 1.5% for related infrastructure like cyberwarfare, though Trump said the U.S. doesn't need to reach the full threshold since it already spends about 3.4% on defense. Trump maintained his cordial but ambiguous stance on NATO's mutual defense commitments \- While offering a surprisingly friendly tone toward the alliance he has long criticized, Trump cast doubt on whether the U.S. would honor Article 5's mutual defense clause, saying "it depends on your definition" and that there are "numerous definitions" of the commitment. The summit highlighted NATO's focus on countering Russian military production despite economic disadvantages \- Rutte emphasized that it's "unthinkable that Russia, with an economy 25 times smaller than NATO's, should be able to outproduce and outgun us," urging European allies to strengthen defenses and increase military production on both sides of the Atlantic. Socialist beats Cuomo in NYC mayoral primary Socialist assemblyman Zohran Mamdani in Tuesday's Democratic mayoral primary, a stunning upset that political analysts called a "political earthquake" signaling the party's leftward shift as younger, progressive voters reshape New York City politics. Mamdani's defeat of Andrew Cuomo signals a major leftward shift in Democratic politics \- The 33-year-old socialist assemblyman decisively beat the former governor, creating a moment for progressives and younger voters to reshape the Democratic Party similar to AOC's 2018 upset victory over Joe Crowley. Socialism and economic populism resonated with young and working class voters despite establishment opposition \- Mamdani's proposals to tax the rich and provide free services like bus fares connected with young voters and working class people, even as he was outspent by Cuomo's $25 million Super PAC and faced opposition from most major labor unions who backed the former governor. The victory creates challenges for Democratic establishment figures and may embolden other socialist challengers \- Party leaders like Governor Kathy Hochul and Senator Chuck Schumer must decide whether to endorse Mamdani, while his win could inspire other democratic socialists to challenge incumbent Democrats in Congress, though his leftist positions on public safety and Israel may hurt him in the general election against Mayor Eric Adams and Republican Curtis Sliwa. Strong opponent to Israel \- Mamdani has expressed strong criticism towards Israel and is in New York. Joe Rogan puts Bernie Sanders in his place for criticizing Elon Musk helping Trump Sen. Bernie Sanders criticized Elon Musk's $270 million donation to Donald Trump's campaign during a Tuesday appearance on "The Joe Rogan Experience," but the podcast host quickly countered by noting Kamala Harris raised $1.5 billion in her losing presidential bid, highlighting how both parties rely on massive donor contributions. Sanders criticized Elon Musk's $270 million donation to Trump while condemning the Citizens United decision \- The Vermont senator called the Supreme Court ruling "maybe the worst decision" ever made and argued it gives billionaires a "constitutional right" to influence elections through massive spending, citing Musk's contributions as an example of the problem. Rogan countered by highlighting Kamala Harris's $1.5 billion campaign spending \- When Sanders attacked Musk's donations, Rogan pointed out that the Harris campaign raised and spent $1.5 billion in just 15 weeks and still ended up $20 million in debt, pointing out that both sides benefit from big money in politics. Sanders acknowledged that both parties rely on billionaire donors despite his criticism \- The self-described democratic socialist admitted he doesn't limit his criticism to Republicans, saying "it wasn't just Musk and the Republicans putting a lot of money into Trump, it was Democratic billionaires putting money into Kamala and other candidates as well." # STOP THE NEEDLESS STEAL OF OUR CURRENT RIGHTS!
---
|
---
| **(SO CALLED) REPUBLICANS IN THE OHIO LEGISLATURE ARE TRYING TO TAKE AWAY YOUR RIGHT TO OPPOSE ZONING DECISIONS BY RAISING THE NUMBER OF SIGNATURES NEEDED FOR CITIZEN-INITIATED BALLOT REFERENDUMS TO AN EXORBITANT LEVEL!**
The Ohio House and Ohio Senate are working to pass their operating budget, identified as HB 96, or House Bill 96.

**The Ohio Senate has amended the Ohio House budget and increased the signatures needed for citizen-initiated zoning referendums from 15% to 35%! This will effectively take away the ability for We The People to put zoning referendums on the ballot. The only way to get rid of this is to tell the members of the House Finance Committee to amend this provision to 15% before the final budget bill is dropped, which will be on or before Monday, June 30.**

Before 2023, the threshold for such a referendum was 8% of the total votes cast in the prior gubernatorial election, but the threshold was raised to 15% in 2023, which was an 87.5% increase. Now they're trying to raise it again to 35% of the total votes cast in the prior gubernatorial election, which is another 133% increase over the current 15% threshold, and a massive 337% increase over the 2023, 8% threshold. Clearly someone wants to force their will on the public regarding zoning issues!

We are asking you to **USE OUR AUTOMATED DIGITAL ACTIVISM SYSTEM** to call, email, and post on the social media of, your State Representative, your State Senator, and members of the Ohio House Finance Committee to let them know that you oppose them voting to approve HB 96 as long as this referendum increase is part of this bill.

You can our "Call To Action" by [**CLICKING HERE & FOLLOWING THE INSTRUCTIONS!**](https://gfiohio.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c2cee5a5358289d5dd20ff17d&id=5350185259&e=5c740fa3e2)

Please SHARE THIS with everyone you can!

# MARCELL STRBICH
FOR OHIO SECRETARY OF STATE
FIRST CAMPAIGN FILING DEADLINE:
**FAST APPROACHING!**
---
|
**MARCELL STRBICH IS RUNNING FOR
OHIO SECRETARY OF STATE
AS A REPUBLICAN POLITICAL OUTSIDER!**
[**strbichforohio.com**](https://gfiohio.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c2cee5a5358289d5dd20ff17d&id=e803b539c6&e=5c740fa3e2)
Many across Ohio already know: Marcell is the right person for this job. He’s a combat veteran, devoted family man, God-fearing patriot, and a proven election integrity advocate. Marcell has been instrumental in drafting nearly every meaningful election integrity bill proposed in Ohio—legislation that’s been deliberately ignored by two consecutive General Assemblies.

Until we see real campaign finance reform, grassroots Ohioans are going to need to dig deep, open their wallets, and be willing to make a personal financial commitment.

_**"In politics, money talks, and campaign filings are how that message gets delivered—loud and clear."**_

It’s important for political candidates to show strong fundraising success in their required government filings because, WHETHER WE LIKE IT OR NOT, money signals momentum, viability, and power—both to insiders and voters. Here’s why it matters:
* Big fundraising numbers make a candidate look like a serious contender. Media, party leaders, donors, and voters all use these filings to gauge who’s competitive and worth taking seriously. Strong fundraising hauls get picked up in headlines: “Candidate Raises $250K in First Quarter”. This creates free publicity and positions the campaign as rising or dominant.
* Party insiders, elected officials, and political organizations often withhold endorsements until they see who can raise money and win. High fundraising can trigger snowball support from power brokers who want to back a winner. Strong numbers can scare off challengers, who may not want to go up against a financially strong opponent.
* Grassroots supporters want to feel they’re backing a campaign that has momentum and a path to victory. Public fundraising reports serve as a psychological boost to volunteers and potential new donors.
* Fundraising equals field operations, advertising, legal support, and more. A candidate who’s raising well is seen as having the infrastructure to compete.

Fundraising filings are more than compliance—they’re performance scorecards. They influence media, endorsements, donor psychology, and even the ballot itself.

**Marcell's first deadline is June 30th.** Shortly after that, his filings are due and the public, including potential donors & the media, will gauge Marcell's financial competitiveness.

**BECAUSE OHIO ONLY REQUIRES A JUNE 30TH AND DECEMBER 31ST FILINGS THIS YEAR, MARCELL WILL NOT HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO SHOW FUNDRAISING MUSCLE TO THE PUBLIC UNTIL 2026!**

**THIS IS WHY IT'S IMPORTANT THAT IF YOU'RE GOING TO DONATE YOU DO IT NOW, AND DONATE AS MUCH AS YOU CAN!**

Here's how to donate:

**DONATE ONLINE:**
[**https://secure.anedot.com/strbichforohio/donate**](https://gfiohio.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c2cee5a5358289d5dd20ff17d&id=682e42a74b&e=5c740fa3e2)

**DONATE BY CHECK:**
**Strbich for Ohio
PO Box 21174
Roanoke, VA 24018**

Please text 614-499-0599 if you need ACH or wire transfer information.

_**Maximum donation is $16,615.67.**_

**THANK YOU! **

More than 150 million Americans have been under heat advisories and warnings this week -- about 45% of the country's population.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b0690f67-4868-4d4b-b232-bf64bc91bc6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Extreme heat is typically defined by two or more days of anomalously high temperatures for a given area. For example, 100°F may not be extreme for the people and infrastructure of southwest Texas, but those living in Maine, a state far less equipped to handle the heat, 100°F could lead to energy system failures and mass casualties.
My slice of Maryland -- just north of Washington DC -- has only seen temperatures this high in June _once in the last 75 years._ ...

subject: We need to have this debate in front of the American public. Add your name if you agree →

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2025 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2025]
Derek, this is incredibly important to me:
If the United States is going to be pulled into a third war in the Middle East, Congress must have this debate in front of the American public.
We need to debate what the stakes are — whether war is in the national interest, and whether the sacrifice we ask of our troops should be the ultimate sacrifice.
Let the American people watch their elected representatives debate the stakes of this prospective war. Let Congress put a war authorization on the table, and let’s debate that . Let’s debate it in front of Virginians, and Kansans and Californians — and hear what our constituents have to say.
Let’s debate that war authorization in the full view of people whose spouses are in the military, or whose kids are in the military. Let’s have that debate in front of every American and hear what they think before we cast a vote that would be one of the most serious votes that you ever cast on the floor of a body like this.
Here is the bottom line: We should not allow a war of the magnitude of this to begin with Congress hiding.
If you agree with me, I’m asking you to sign on to show your support for my war powers resolution that affirms war should not happen without a vote of Congress. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/SK23uTDBxU6baQA2yQTa9g2]
Thank you for reading and staying engaged on this critical issue.
-Tim Kaine

subject: Stand with me to protect public broadcasting
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Dan Goldman for New York**

Peter, Public broadcasting is an essential part of our democracy — one that educates, informs, and inspires millions of Americans every day. **But House Republicans rubber stamped Donald Trump’s all-out assault on public broadcasting and independent media.** Recently, House Republicans opposed my amendment to stop President Trump from completely defunding the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, which supports essential independent media and forms of accountability, as well as children’s educational programs and emergency alert systems. Instead of supporting programs and services vital to the American people, Republicans have once again bent the knee to Donald Trump. I won’t stand by and watch as they attempt to silence one of the most trusted sources of news and educational programming. Public broadcasting isn’t just TV and radio. **It's a lifeline for countless families, providing resources for teachers and educational content for children. It’s a platform for diverse voices and stories. **An attack on public broadcasting is an attack on democracy. Full stop. I am committed to defending public broadcasting and ensuring it remains a stronghold of independent journalism. **But I can't do it alone.** I need your help to send a strong message to those who aim to dismantle it. **[Join me in standing up for our First Amendment and essential public broadcasting by signing my petition today:](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110220493/553652660/-187622752?refcode=AU_DSG_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20250625_AM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85NDA4NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZmQ1YjkzNi1kMTUxLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=SMAqq9xuqIpXZyikL4_88j9N53NyqZiztherWBY8d5k=&emci=ddfc7e12-a650-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=1fd5b936-d151-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=13556823)** | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110220494/553652661/-187622752?refcode=AU_DSG_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20250625_AM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85NDA4NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZmQ1YjkzNi1kMTUxLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=SMAqq9xuqIpXZyikL4_88j9N53NyqZiztherWBY8d5k=&emci=ddfc7e12-a650-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=1fd5b936-d151-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=13556823)

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: Naysayers said it would never happen.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
After nearly 30 years of inaction, our elected officials found the courage to act.
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-june25.m4W6Vr&refcode=em250624-1-b&t=1&akid=10611%2E3935704%2EFN6DFd)
Team --
Today marks three years since President Biden signed the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act into law.
It took months of tough negotiations and an initial procedural vote. Naysayers said it would never happen. For decades, the gun lobby fought hard to prevent that day from happening.
But after nearly 30 years of inaction, our elected officials found the courage to act. Our movement for gun safety worked tirelessly to get this over the finish line, and it has had a real impact on our efforts to save lives.
This was an important first step in our work, but we cannot let that momentum stop.**Right now, the Trump Administration is directly targeting and trying to dismantle key pieces of the BSCA -- things we KNOW have helped save lives. The urgency is real, and we can’t go back. **
No other developed nation in the world experiences this level of gun violence. Too many lives have been robbed because of it. We owe it to our country to fix our broken system and make sure nobody goes through this heartbreak again.
[**GIFFORDS works year-round to invest in communities, elect gun safety leaders, and secure a safer world for us all. Our end-of-quarter deadline is in 5 days. We’re excited to invite you to Part 3 of our Families First educational series, a timely conversation about inflation, work
incentives, and the urgent need for family tax relief that reflects today’s economic reality.

This episode, “Why Family Tax Relief Must Keep Up With the Cost of Living,” features:

• Debbie Kraulidis, Vice President of Moms for America

• Leah Sargeant, policy fellow at the Niskanen Center and author of the forthcoming book The Dignity of Dependence

• Mercedes Schlapp, conservative media personality and former White House senior advisor

Together, they explore why the current $2,000 Child Tax Credit, set in 2017, is worth far less today, and how smart reforms can
reward work, support families, and strengthen the American workforce. You’ll also hear about how this moment ties into the
permanent extension of the 45S paid family leave tax credit, a key pro-family, pro-business provision currently being debated in
Congress.

[] [] [] Inflation is Rising – The Value of Tax Relief Must Rise With It! SUPPORT THE BIG, BEAUTIFUL BILL: Secure the Child Tax Credit Families are Being Squeezed and the tax policy hasn't kept up. We’re excited to invite you to Part 3 of our Families First educational series, a timely conversation about inflation, work incentives, and the urgent need for family tax relief that reflects today’s economic reality. This episode, “Why Family Tax Relief Must Keep Up With the Cost of Living,” features: • Debbie Kraulidis, Vice President of Moms for America • Leah Sargeant, policy fellow at the Niskanen Center and author of the forthcoming book The Dignity of Dependence • Mercedes Schlapp, conservative media personality and former White House senior advisor Together, they explore why the current $2,000 Child Tax Credit, set in 2017, is worth far less today, and how smart reforms can reward work, support families, and strengthen the American workforce. You’ll also hear about how this moment ties into the permanent extension of the 45S paid family leave tax credit, a key pro-family, pro-business provision currently being debated in Congress. Leah’s upcoming book, The Dignity of Dependence [] (releasing this fall), highlights many of the themes we cover – offering a thoughtful look at how good policy can support both work and care without compromising conservative values. WATCH THE VIDEO [] Watch now and stay informed on how tax policy is shaping the future for America's families. Peter,

My name is Adam Schwarze, and if this is your first time hearing from me, let me introduce myself.

I was born in St. Paul, Minnesota, in 1983 and adopted by Joel and Deb Schwarze when I was six months old. I grew up in Bloomington, where hockey was more than a pastime—it was a foundation for leadership and teamwork.

After the terrorist attacks on 9/11, I felt a deep calling to serve. **On my 18th birthday in October 2001, I enlisted as an infantryman in the United States Marine Corps. I deployed with the 1st Marine Division during Operation Iraqi Freedom, earning multiple valor and meritorious promotions awards.**

In 2013, I achieved my lifelong ambition by becoming a **Navy SEAL Officer, serving with SEAL Team Three and later joining the elite undersea-focused enterprise of U.S. Special Operations Command.** Over my 21-year military career, I deployed nine times to over 70 countries, conducting combat, intelligence, and humanitarian missions.

Now, I'm stepping up to serve Minnesota in a new capacity—as a Republican candidate for U.S. Senate.

**The Stakes in This Race Are Enormous.**

I'm running against **Tim Walz’s lieutenant governor** , who is even more radical than he is. While Minneapolis was burning during the 2020 riots, she wasn't defending the people or supporting the police—she was preparing a lawsuit _**against**_ the Minneapolis Police Department.

Governor Walz wants America to believe **Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents are the Gestapo.** His words, not mine. And this is who they call a “moderate.”

So ask yourself: _**If this is what their moderates sound like, what is their real agenda?**_

**Every time the left doesn't get their way, they call Republicans Nazis.**

Every time we demand border security or want criminal illegal aliens deported, they call us bigots.

But you know better—and so do I. Enforcing immigration law is not hateful.**It's common sense**. It's about **protecting Americans**.

**Here's What I Believe:** I believe that no one is above the law—especially criminal illegal aliens who commit rape, murder, and violence against American citizens.

I believe in a **strong border, deporting those who break our laws, and respecting the rule of law** —no exceptions, no apologies.

I believe that veterans, police officers, working families, and law-abiding Americans deserve a voice in the Senate—not professional politicians who mock us and ignore our communities.

**I've Never Run for Office Before. That's the Point.**

Unlike my opponent, I wasn't groomed for politics. I joined the military on my 18th birthday—October 2001—just weeks after the attacks on our homeland. I didn't run from duty. I ran toward it.

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

Colorado Activist Group Blocks ICE From Arresting Accused Child Rapist
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
We apologize for the odd timing of our newsletter this week, we're having some technical difficulties behind-the-scenes. We hope you still enjoy!

Listen to today's Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)! Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** From rising costs to rising outrage, Coloradans are feeling the pressure. The state [DMV just raised fees](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), some homeowners are now paying an average of $440/month for insurance—with the [sixth-highest homeowners insurance premiums](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in the nation, and bureaucratic [green energy mandates](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) could cost ratepayers $45 billion. A new [lawsuit over emissions standards](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) is drawing fire from the trucking industry as unworkable and wasteful.
Meanwhile, ICE agents say an [anti-ICE activist group](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in Colorado helped a fugitive accused of child rape evade arrest, igniting a fresh clash over sanctuary policies. And in Denver, [hacked traffic signs](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) displaying anti-ICE messages have raised questions about digital security on public infrastructure.
🇺🇸 **On the National Stage...** President Trump announced a [historic ceasefire agreement between Iran and Israel](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), marking the end of the 12-day war that threatened to destabilize the Middle East. The deal, coordinated with help from Qatar and U.S. officials, was praised as a major diplomatic win that avoided further escalation without U.S. military involvement.
This is the Mountain Minute for Wednesday, June 25, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado Activist Group Blocks ICE From Arresting Accused Child Rapist](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER GAZETTE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Federal immigration agents on Friday attempting to arrest a Salvadoran fugitive accused of child rape in Italy were thwarted when an anti-ICE group allegedly alerted him of the raid, allowing him to evade capture, federal authorities.
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents on Saturday accused members of the Colorado Rapid Response Network on social media of interfering in the attempted arrest of Jose Reyes Leon-Deras.
“Groups like this interfere with ICE’s ability to keep communities safe,” ICE said in an X post Saturday. “Thanks to Colorado Rapid Response members, a fugitive child rapist evaded our arrest.
“We target specific aliens for GOOD reasons! Do YOU want a child rapist in your neighborhood?!”
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Trucking industry: Colorado’s climate lawsuit is unrealistic and wasteful](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Colorado’s trucking industry is pushing back against a lawsuit filed by Attorney General Phil Weiser challenging federal limits on stricter vehicle emissions standards, calling the effort unrealistic and politically motivated.
* Industry leaders argue the California-style emissions targets adopted by Colorado are “impossible” to meet—especially for large vehicles in cold climates—and that electric trucks are not yet viable statewide.
* The Colorado Motor Carriers Association says the state ignored their proposals for more practical emissions solutions, like renewable natural gas, in favor of costly mandates on electric vehicles.

|

**[Who’s controlling the signs? Denver traffic boards hacked with anti-ICE F-bomb](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [WESTWORD](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* A Denver traffic sign near I-25 was hacked on June 22 to display “Bring the Heat F*** ICE,” sparking alarm and confusion among drivers and city officials.
* The Denver Department of Transportation confirmed a lock on the sign’s controller panel was broken, allowing someone outside the project to change the message.
* Although DOTI claims only one sign was affected, locals reported seeing similar messages elsewhere, raising broader questions about messaging security and political tensions over immigration enforcement.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

name: Dan Crenshaw
subject: Do you want to kill the cartels?
body:
President Trump's delivering on his promise
| | | | | | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JYKXBD7Q73PR65620SE87DP9_0)
---
| | | | Peter, Me: “Do you want to kill cartels?”

President Trump: “I definitely want to kill cartels” That’s what President Trump told me at Mar-a-Lago just days before his second term began. Six months in, he's delivered on that promise. Border crossings are at record lows. For the first time in years, Mexico City is going hard after cartels. And I’ve been named Chairman of the Cartel Task Force in Congress-working directly with the Trump Administration to develop aggressive new tactics that will dismantle the cartels for good. The Mexican drug cartels are the number one threat to the United States. The brutal tactics used by terrorist groups in Iraq and Afghanistan—the same ones I fought against—were modeled after cartels like Sinaloa and CJNG. This is a war, and we’re bringing the full weight of American power to win it. But here’s the truth: defeating the cartels won’t happen overnight. It’s going to take years. And I’m ready to see it through—every step of the way. I’m in Congress for this mission. But I can’t do it alone. I’m up against a crowded, well-funded primary. And our End of Quarter deadline is June 30. If you want someone in Congress with the experience and will to finish this fight, I need your help now. **[Please donate before the June 30 deadline and stand with me in the fight to destroy the cartels once and for all.](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JYKXBD7Q73PR65620SE87DP9_1)**

It strips health care from millions by slashing Medicaid and gutting the Affordable Care Act. It cuts funding for SNAP, forcing families to go hungry. It pulls critical funding from hospitals, threatening to close those, especially in rural communities. And it incentivizes companies to offshore American jobs.
_And it’s all to fund tax handouts for billionaires._
I didn’t come to Congress to serve Trump or rubber-stamp his agenda. I’m here to fight for you — for working families, for union jobs, for good health care, and for the basic idea that government should work for the people, not just the powerful.
Trump and his Republican allies are betting that we’ll sit this one out. That we’re too tired, too discouraged, or too outspent to push back. That just because we don’t have the majority, we won’t fight.
_Let’s prove them wrong._
Let’s show them we’re ready to stand strong — for health care, for workers, and for a government that actually gives a damn about people.

body:
Did you know poll workers in PA are elected?

| | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=JgyyvCfQwldlSeD7KJl_Ih7269o_4hwqOhPs1_PHvgI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=judge_of_elections_recruitment&n=1)
---
| Peter -- As dedicated advocates for democracy and fair elections, we have a unique opportunity to protect the process. Did you know that Pennsylvania is the only state in the nation where poll workers are elected? This means that the role of Judge of Elections is crucial for ensuring the integrity of our electoral process, yet it often goes uncontested or left vacant. We are reaching out to encourage you to consider running for the Judge of Elections position. This four-year term requires only a two-day commitment each year: one for the primary election and one for the general election. There is also state sponsored training. This is a great way to directly contribute to a smooth and fair election process in your community. If you’re interested in exploring this opportunity further, we invite you to book an appointment with our recruitment expert. They can provide you with all the information you need to make an informed decision about running. Your participation could make a significant difference in upholding the democratic process in Pennsylvania. Let’s work together to ensure our elections are represented by dedicated individuals who care about the integrity of our system. | [](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=pw8xxFOT77yeHOCsPcLemOFomft6-yQn8d5cOOo16xQJnkGI0UtNnWCu962Z-5JW&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=judge_of_elections_recruitment&n=2 "Book an appointment!") name: Sarah McBride
subject: A personal note for you
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Nevada State Democratic Party, NVDEMS
body:
I know how easy it is to feel discouraged. I’ve felt it too. | | | Hi friend, it’s Congresswoman Sarah McBride. When I was growing up, I couldn’t imagine a future like mine. I worried that the heart of this country wasn’t big enough to love someone like me. But over the years, I’ve witnessed change that once felt unimaginable — and because of voters in my home state of Delaware and supporters across the country, I became the first openly transgender member elected to Congress last November. I’m carrying that with me this Pride Month. **Because Pride teaches us that hope matters most when it’s hard.** Right now, it’s a frightening time for so many in our country. LGBTQ+ people, especially trans youth, are being targeted with cruelty — online, in our communities, and by politicians in Congress. I know how easy it is to feel discouraged. I’ve felt it too. But we must remember that Pride was born at Stonewall in resistance, in protest, and in the belief that even in the face of fear, change is still possible. **That’s why it’s more important than ever to fight for what’s right.** To stay rooted in our values and our vision. And just as importantly, to keep believing that through the power of our proximity, we can bring more people along. **But we won’t get there alone. It’s going to take all of us building a movement strong enough to meet this moment and carry us forward.[_So if you’re ready to do your part, please split a $3 donation between my campaign and the Nevada Democratic Party now._](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu4ksFa5SF7IXH6Sr7Lz9yTSc6VWQyrIEwcklXwav9inEye1Tig3jDGPlTg6yK_iupWn8DlVOKnA5HddfA4r3G6UI1yacTh7zNsWHcMAG9b7fJURhGdGLdc_tNvmegU9heylfiwlUTMhQCy0YanmWc_iPMIoSSB92KG1DAa5Nqr5Z2r_sVQguO6Tt1fsNzZZSptClb4oY9YAAId8Jnu995VXSJrfigOqZ3WxWIKXP81ouAXJZ7ue4NKm7UvwiJ61gzmRT6CSgeNGy-aNXtUgj6IoIXFygtRhhwuoiEAGyA2AvoCQ3c_GKgMzO-GzL9xs3yu2e7bMIgr7G7V5wWIG2CGqJ6wvU2MeWrOITmiKji_5icYnLK92aBr4Ynn82xKlCohziiYMmwU28wSq8ONqrjkyqD3fIb3KoIcCkHBSvMu0qQ-VdweII7MIrh4iv6kfz6mG5Z0Fwsu4FExstypWfMR/4hn/xFxtkK2cSSCS-swpta7VBg/h0/h001.MUihkUdiRGFh2okOKhCagNAKIgnPgUK4LH7v0ZrD8MY)** I know a better tomorrow is possible if we put in the work. clean_body: I know how easy it is to feel discouraged. I’ve felt it too. | | | Hi friend, it’s Congresswoman Sarah McBride. When I was growing up, I couldn’t imagine a future like mine. I worried that the heart of this country wasn’t big enough to love someone like me. But over the years, I’ve witnessed change that once felt unimaginable — and because of voters in my home state of Delaware and supporters across the country, I became the first openly transgender member elected to Congress last November. I’m carrying that with me this Pride Month. Because Pride teaches us that hope matters most when it’s hard. Right now, it’s a frightening time for so many in our country. LGBTQ+ people, especially trans youth, are being targeted with cruelty — online, in our communities, and by politicians in Congress. I know how easy it is to feel discouraged. I’ve felt it too. But we must remember that Pride was born at Stonewall in resistance, in protest, and in the belief that even in the face of fear, change is still possible. That’s why it’s more important than ever to fight for what’s right. To stay rooted in our values and our vision. And just as importantly, to keep believing that through the power of our proximity, we can bring more people along. But we won’t get there alone. It’s going to take all of us building a movement strong enough to meet this moment and carry us forward. I know a better tomorrow is possible if we put in the work. In solidarity and Happy Pride, Sarah | The Nevada State Democratic Party fights for progress in the Silver State. #
---
---
**Sarah**
