Make no mistake, Peter: Republicans are still coming for our rights. |
---
[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110247909/553732272/-1686146655?refcode=WUEFE663_20250625_JMOpEdRS_ALL&sourceid=1056445&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2OTJkN2EyZi0wMDUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=F4Lg80mls2rO9-5aTz98r2TXzMn8SpTnW8-NRL5OywM=) Yesterday marked three years since the U.S. Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , ending the constitutional right to abortion in this country and stripping away the fundamental freedoms of millions of American women.

Since then, a 13-year-old in Mississippi was forced to give birth. A brain-dead woman in Georgia was kept on life support to carry a pregnancy against her family's will. And doctors are still being forced to deny care to women on the brink of death.

This is the world Republicans created. And they're not done yet. | [HELP STOP ANTI-CHOICE EXTREMISM](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110247910/553732273/-1686146655?refcode=WUEFE663_20250625_JMOpEdRS_ALL&sourceid=1056445&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2OTJkN2EyZi0wMDUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=F4Lg80mls2rO9-5aTz98r2TXzMn8SpTnW8-NRL5OywM=)
---
Now, in the third year since that devastating decision, Donald Trump is president again. And things are getting even worse.

Just weeks ago, Trump rescinded federal guidance requiring hospitals to provide emergency abortion care to pregnant patients when their lives are at risk. His administration is actively creating confusion and fear among doctors who are trying to do their jobs. And it's putting lives on the line.

At the same time, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is now calling on the FDA to re-review its approval of mifepristone — a safe and effective medication used in more than 60% of abortions nationwide — based on a junk science report from a right-wing think tank. If he succeeds, it could effectively ban abortion access _in blue and red states alike_.

clean_body: Make no mistake, Peter: Republicans are still coming for our rights. | = Yesterday marked three years since the U.S. Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade , ending the constitutional right to abortion in this country and stripping away the fundamental freedoms of millions of American women. Since then, a 13-year-old in Mississippi was forced to give birth. A brain-dead woman in Georgia was kept on life support to carry a pregnancy against her family's will. And doctors are still being forced to deny care to women on the brink of death. This is the world Republicans created. And they're not done yet. | = Now, in the third year since that devastating decision, Donald Trump is president again. And things are getting even worse. Just weeks ago, Trump rescinded federal guidance requiring hospitals to provide emergency abortion care to pregnant patients when their lives are at risk. His administration is actively creating confusion and fear among doctors who are trying to do their jobs. And it's putting lives on the line. At the same time, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is now calling on the FDA to re-review its approval of mifepristone — a safe and effective medication used in more than 60% of abortions nationwide — based on a junk science report from a right-wing think tank. If he succeeds, it could effectively ban abortion access in blue and red states alike. And in Congress, anti-choice Republicans snuck last-minute anti-abortion provisions into their latest budget bill — targeting states that actually protect the right to choose. **= That's why EMILYs List launched Mission Majority , our plan to take back control of the U.S. House in 2026 by replacing 46 extreme anti-choice incumbent Republicans with Democratic pro-choice women. We know it’s possible because we've done it before — and with your help, we can do it again. We cannot sit back and let Trump, RFK Jr., and congressional Republicans keep waging this war on our rights. Mitch McConnell doesn’t care.
**Mitch McConnell Says People Worried About Medicaid Cuts Will 'Get Over It'
\- _Newsweek_** Peter,

Medicaid covers one third of Kentuckians, half of Kentucky kids, and 70% of the long term care costs our seniors rely on. The bill that Republicans are negotiating in the Senate will gut this coverage and threaten rural healthcare all over the country.

And what does Kentucky Senator Mitch McConnell, in a closed-door meeting with other Republican senators, have to say about this?

**“I know a lot of us are hearing from people back home about Medicaid. But they’ll get over it.”**

Folks, 16 million Americans are going to lose their healthcare if this bill becomes law. What McConnell said is callous and cruel.

This is not what leadership looks like. As I’ve said many times, our elected leaders should make decisions with the best interests of their people in mind.

I’m fighting for better leadership here in Kentucky and across the country, because we can’t allow people in Washington to keep passing laws that hurt people. Medicaid keeps Kentuckians and people in all 50 states alive, keeps them healthy, and makes sure they have a doctor or a hospital to go to when they or a loved one gets sick.

On May 5, 2025, attorney **Matt Benda** appeared before the Minnesota Supreme Court in _Benda for Common-sense v. Minnesota Secretary of State (A23-0302)_ to challenge the legality of embedded modems in election machines.
> "Every voter's vote is entitled to be counted once. It must be correctly counted and reported." -- quoting _Gray v. Sanders_ ,
Benda opened his argument with a powerful call to uphold the dignity of counting and reporting votes correctly.
> "Voting has evolved rapidly from the simple process of dropping a ballot in a box on Election Day to a complex framework where voting starts weeks in advance and electronic machines are used almost exclusively to accept, tally and report vote totals.
> The on-going evolution of "voting" justifies dynamic scrutiny of the entire process to protect the dignity of "counting and reporting votes correctly."
He declared in an open court of law that **Rice County, and at least six other Minnesota counties** have voting machines with embedded modems which connect to the internet. Such fact is a clear violation of **Minn. Stat. § 206.845**, which states:
> _" No connection by modem is permitted."_
Benda also emphasized his argument that modems qualify as part of a "voting system" under **Minn. Stat. § 206.57**, yet **have not been properly certified** as required by law. In arguing for dynamic scrutiny of electronic voting systems, he warned:
> "Eventually, there will be some type of snafu... Either the power goes down, data is lost or compromised, or in a worst-case scenario -- a bad actor infiltrates our election process."
Addressing the appellate court's procedural ruling on service of process, Benda criticized what he called a **" drive-by jurisdictional ruling,"** noting that under their interpretation, over **130 candidates** would have needed personal service--_" including three of you sitting here today."_
In a surprise development, in the opening moments (starting at 5:12) of oral arguments, Chief Justice Natalie Hudson stated, "you make persuasive arguments, I think, in your brief that the [service of process part of] the statute is really more of a claims processing provision which would suggest that it goes to personal jurisdiction as opposed to subject-matter jurisdiction." This was not expected as the classification of the service requirement as a subject-matter jurisdiction process was the sole basis relied upon by the Minnesota Court of Appeals in dismissing this case.1

The Minnesota Supreme Court appears poised to reverse the Court of Appeals' published opinion on this jurisdictional quesiton. Securing initial jurisdiction, however, is only the first step toward achieving full judicial scrutiny of modem usage in Minnesota elections.
The Supreme Court asked whether the delay in this case had effectively made the action moot, or too late to proceed. In response, Benda argued that the modem question for the 2026 election is the same as it was for the 2024 election. The parties have already created a strong record upon which the district court proceedings could be launched. Benda urged the Court to reverse the Court of Appeals' decision and remand the case to district court:
> "The election officials in this case have made every attempt to stagnate scrutiny... Voters look to this Court to help us find a path where public checks and balances evolve."
The full oral argument is available on the Minnesota Judicial Branch website - [HERE](https://substack.com/redirect/77f5b961-d3b3-49aa-9b69-95a40bfa5fbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). There is no deadline for the Court to issue its order, but past practice suggests that a ruling should be issued later this summer.
If this case is remanded, Benda For Common-sense must be ready to finalize the engagement of expert witnesses and other case preparations. body:
Protecting and advancing the VRA is at the forefront of the fight for fair maps. Here’s why:
| [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110248827/553735282/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjk5YjVhNjI5LTAzNTItZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=dIb0mwrpgROvW7sJVwlmbIng0Tn1teN6eMKxcx4IfgE=&emci=18b3c232-2b51-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=99b5a629-0352-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=8431045)
---

Hey Peter, 12 years ago, the Supreme Court’s _Shelby County_ ruling effectively gutted Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act (VRA), making it easier for states to erect barriers to the right to vote for communities of color. This section of the VRA protected against suppressive and discriminatory voting legislation by requiring certain states and local governments with a history of racial bias to obtain federal approval of any changes to election laws, a process known as “preclearance.” **Unfortunately, Peter, we’ve seen the consequences firsthand when checks and balances and essential oversight are stripped away.** **Just take a look at Texas: **On the day of the _Shelby County_ ruling, lawmakers in Texas declared that they would move forward in executing the nation’s most restrictive voter ID law that was originally blocked. _And they certainly did._ Since then, Texas has faced various legal challenges due to extreme partisan and racial gerrymandering. And fast forward to today, _LULAC v. Abbott_ is currently being heard in federal court due to the state’s congressional maps being challenged for intentionally discriminating against Black and Latino voters. **But the NDRC is fighting back — whether it’s sounding the alarm on racial and partisan gerrymandering, or helping to elect Democracy Defenders, the NDRC is on the frontlines in the fight for fair maps. **[**Rush a donation to help advance the NDRC’s efforts to protect the right to vote, safeguard our democracy, and ensure free and fair elections.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110248828/553735283/1950963963?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_ShelbyCountyAnniversary_email_20250625-NDRC-Tier1-ShelbyCountyAnniversary_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250625-NDRC-Tier1-ShelbyCountyAnniversary_&utm_campaign=ShelbyCountyAnniversary&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjk5YjVhNjI5LTAzNTItZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=dIb0mwrpgROvW7sJVwlmbIng0Tn1teN6eMKxcx4IfgE=) [DONATE](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110248829/553735284/1950963963?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_ShelbyCountyAnniversary_email_20250625-NDRC-Tier1-ShelbyCountyAnniversary_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250625-NDRC-Tier1-ShelbyCountyAnniversary_&utm_campaign=ShelbyCountyAnniversary&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjk5YjVhNjI5LTAzNTItZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=dIb0mwrpgROvW7sJVwlmbIng0Tn1teN6eMKxcx4IfgE=) The _Shelby County_ decision handed unscrupulous elected officials the perfect opportunity to silence voters, manipulate maps, and advance an anti-democracy agenda. After this ruling, there was a rise in anti-voter policies that made it more difficult for people to cast their ballots. Just right next door, Louisiana has followed Texas’s lead. **As early as tomorrow morning, the Supreme Court will issue a decision regarding Louisiana’s previous maps — maps that were racially gerrymandered and undermine the voting power of Black Louisianans.** When a federal court found that Louisiana’s old maps likely violated the VRA, the maps were then redrawn to create two Black opportunity districts in the state, empowering Louisianians to finally have fair representation. But then, anti-democracy forces filed a lawsuit to get rid of the new, fairer map. So you see Peter, protecting and advancing the VRA to build a truly representative democracy is why we do what we do at the NDRC. **While the far-right relentlessly and unfairly consolidate power and minimize the voting power of Black and brown communities in states across the country, we’re leading the fight for fair maps because of the need to stop partisan gerrymander efforts by the GOP.** [**We have to be prepared for whatever comes next — and we know that extremists will stop at nothing to get what they want. Will you contribute $30 or whatever you can to the NDRC so we can continue fighting against map manipulation?**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110248830/553735285/1950963963?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_ShelbyCountyAnniversary_email_20250625-NDRC-Tier1-ShelbyCountyAnniversary_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250625-NDRC-Tier1-ShelbyCountyAnniversary_&utm_campaign=ShelbyCountyAnniversary&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjk5YjVhNjI5LTAzNTItZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=dIb0mwrpgROvW7sJVwlmbIng0Tn1teN6eMKxcx4IfgE=) | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

clean_body: Protecting and advancing the VRA is at the forefront of the fight for fair maps. Here’s why: | Hey Peter, 12 years ago, the Supreme Court’s Shelby County ruling effectively gutted Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act (VRA), making it easier for states to erect barriers to the right to vote for communities of color. This section of the VRA protected against suppressive and discriminatory voting legislation by requiring certain states and local governments with a history of racial bias to obtain federal approval of any changes to election laws, a process known as “preclearance.” Unfortunately, Peter, we’ve seen the consequences firsthand when checks and balances and essential oversight are stripped away. Just take a look at Texas: On the day of the Shelby County ruling, lawmakers in Texas declared that they would move forward in executing the nation’s most restrictive voter ID law that was originally blocked. And they certainly did. Since then, Texas has faced various legal challenges due to extreme partisan and racial gerrymandering. And fast forward to today, LULAC v. Abbott is currently being heard in federal court due to the state’s congressional maps being challenged for intentionally discriminating against Black and Latino voters. But the NDRC is fighting back — whether it’s sounding the alarm on racial and partisan gerrymandering, or helping to elect Democracy Defenders, the NDRC is on the frontlines in the fight for fair maps. = = The Shelby County decision handed unscrupulous elected officials the perfect opportunity to silence voters, manipulate maps, and advance an anti-democracy agenda. After this ruling, there was a rise in anti-voter policies that made it more difficult for people to cast their ballots. Just right next door, Louisiana has followed Texas’s lead. As early as tomorrow morning, the Supreme Court will issue a decision regarding Louisiana’s previous maps — maps that were racially gerrymandered and undermine the voting power of Black Louisianans. When a federal court found that Louisiana’s old maps likely violated the VRA, the maps were then redrawn to create two Black opportunity districts in the state, empowering Louisianians to finally have fair representation. But then, anti-democracy forces filed a lawsuit to get rid of the new, fairer map. So you see Peter, protecting and advancing the VRA to build a truly representative democracy is why we do what we do at the NDRC. body:
I’ve spent my entire life serving this country, and I’m not about to stop now. I’m going to keep standing up, doing what I think is right — you can be sure of that.
#

Team,
There’s a lot going on right now. Too much.
I get it if you’d rather tune it out. Really, I do. But please, let me try and remind you why we have to stay in the fight.
After Gabby was shot, it wasn’t easy. We didn’t know if she would make it, if she would ever talk or walk again.
But her doctors, nurses, and therapists never gave up on her.
In the months and years afterwards, the recovery was hard. It was tough on Gabby. But she never gave up, and I wasn’t going to give up, either.
We kept going. We didn’t quit. We didn’t back down.
It’s hard to see the path forward, sometimes. But with the help of your friends and family, you find a way. For Gabby and I, this team has always been a part of that. Knowing that we have people like you in our corner has given us a lot of hope in difficult moments.
That support has meant the world to me. And it has shown me that together, we can do really big things.
I’ve spent my entire life serving this country, and I’m not about to stop now. I’m going to keep standing up, doing what I think is right — you can be sure of that.
But I can’t do this work alone.
[**Between Elon Musk, Roger Stone, even Trump himself, we’ve got some powerful people lining up against us. And to keep the fight up, I’m asking if you’ll make a donation to my campaign.**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-june25/.u07CFH&refcode=em250625-1-600&t=1&akid=6092%2E6688874%2EWh6ebO)

**Mike Nellis joined Don Lemon this afternoon to unpack one of the most surprising political upsets in recent memory: Zohran Mamdani 's apparent victory over Andrew Cuomo in the NYC Democratic mayoral primary.**
In a candid and wide-ranging conversation, Nellis and Lemon dove into the campaign dynamics that led to Mamdani's surge--and Cuomo's collapse. Nellis described Mamdani's campaign as one of the most focused and effective of the cycle, emphasizing affordability, local impact, and real coalition-building. They discussed how Mamdani met voters where they are, cut through the noise, and channeled the kind of authenticity and urgency that so many Democratic candidates struggle to find.
They also examined how Cuomo's arrogance, lack of ground game, and failure to adapt to a new political landscape helped doom his chances--even with name recognition and a cash advantage. Ranked-choice voting and NYC's public financing laws helped level the field, but it was Mamdani's clarity of message and coalition savvy that sealed the deal.
But the conversation wasn't just about this one race. Nellis and Lemon explored the broader implications for the Democratic Party: why candidates who actually seem like they _give a damn_ are winning, and why voters across the spectrum are willing to take risks when traditional leaders stop delivering. They cautioned against overcorrecting or drawing the wrong lessons--this wasn't a socialist wave, and it wasn't the end of the establishment. But it _was_ a sign that young, bold, disciplined leadership is breaking through.
They also covered:
- Whether Eric Adams can mount a general election comeback
- Why Mamdani is more Michelle Wu than Brandon Johnson
- The strategic use of social media and small-dollar energy
- The divide between performative politics and real impact
- What other rising candidates--like Mallory McMorrow and Jake Rakov--can learn from this moment
- And how voters are increasingly following people, not parties or institutions
The discussion closed with a bigger takeaway about media itself. As trust in traditional outlets collapses, voices like Lemon's and Nellis's--rooted in authenticity, independence, and real-world experience--are resonating with a public that's tired of spin and hungry for truth.

_**The NYC Democrat mayoral primary yesterday proved how a radical and well organized group of "Democrat Socialists" could take an election. The breakdown of the voters is even more frightening but mimics any No Kings Rally or anti-Elon protest.**_
Here is the breakdown:

It was the "yuppie" white social justice warriors that pushed Zohran over the edge, including liberal Jews that were for Zohran, despite his BDS stance and anti-Israel stance.

This was Jim's Response to October 7th.
_**Unfortunately, being pro-Israel and being a democrat are becoming mutually exclusive positions as these politicians show up at rallies to fight antisemitism and stand up for Israel and then do something completely different.**_
**What Can You Do?**
Demand Accountability and judge a politician by their actions - their words are meaningless.
Guys like Sid Rosenberg have been warning NYC for a long time and he was right on Mamdani. The challenge is will enough New Yorkers get it by November. What will it take? Grocery Stores having shut downs in protest of Mamdani - Gristedes Owner John Catsimatidis has threatened to close all stores if Mamdani wins. What will landlords do with Rent Freezes as property taxes will increase to subsidize the unfunded socialist programs of Mamdani and his cohort of Democrat Socialists.
**Where does NYC Go From here?**
It's gonna have to shake itself out quickly for a sensible attack on Mamdani this November as - IT IS TIME TO MESS WITH THE ZOHRAN.
The mayoral field will either stay wide or one anti-Zohran candidate will emerge for a lesser of two evils with whatever back-door concessions are needed to get unified buy-in.
**Who will be the front-runner?**
If NYC is ready for a Republican like Curtis Sliwa, then he will be the leader, OR all roads will converge to Adams or some other line that Cuomo will run on.
_**Sensible Democrats voted for Cuomo but a divided field of apathetic voters this November may result in Mamdani if the voters and the candidates are not united (which they are currently not).**_
**Connecticut - Wake Up**
There are plenty of Zohran Mamdani's running this state and they almost got their way because of HB 5002. The only reason why Lamont vetoed this is because he is likely to run for re-election next year and his veto is a demonstration that he is not as "woke" as the rest of his progressives in the Statehouse.
While the rest of the country is becoming more centrist and conservative New York and Connecticut have been going in the opposite direction.
Socialism fails wherever it is implemented. Irrational green energy policies which ignore, increased nuclear energy, and easy access to, the cleanest and most cost-effective fossil fuel, natural gas, will never result in affordable and available energy.
Our towns have evolved on their own for over three centuries. Local control has been an essential part of Connecticut Democracy. The Zohrans of this world want it to come to an end. Say no at the ballot box.
In 2025 we have town wide elections. In 2026 we elect the governor, state officials, state legislators, and congressman.
The future of Connecticut depends on these elections. We must fight back against the Socialist, Communist progressive liberal candidates by electing rational conservatives.

President Donald Trump alongside Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth **[got into a tense exchange with a reporter](https://substack.com/redirect/6b4f8c66-a3bc-49f1-b806-f02afdb9579f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Wednesday who questioned the efficacy of U.S. military strikes on Iran nuclear facilities and whether they actually "obliterated" Iran's nuclear armaments as the president says.
"Oh here we go..." Trump sighed, annoyed. "It's been obliterated Kelly!"
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/6b4f8c66-a3bc-49f1-b806-f02afdb9579f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/6b4f8c66-a3bc-49f1-b806-f02afdb9579f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"Mr. President, you talked about expecting some on-the-ground assessments at Fordow and the other sites, is that Israeli and U.S. ..." the reporter began to ask Trump.
"It's been obliterated Kelly!" Trump interjected, tired of the mainstream media doubting the success of his strikes last weekend. "Totally obliterated!"
The reporter cited **[an intelligence report](https://substack.com/redirect/bf6d90d4-7145-470d-aa21-799ff2526316?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** suggesting that Iran's nuclear facilities were not definitively destroyed by the strikes.
"People like you picked it up and said 'oh it's not severe.' No, the report was not a complete report," the president fired back.
Trump, frustrated by the reporter, **[turned the podium over to Hegseth to respond](https://substack.com/redirect/6b4f8c66-a3bc-49f1-b806-f02afdb9579f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to the question.
"There's a reason the president calls out fake news for what it is!" Hegseth scolded the reporter. "The instinct of CNN, the instinct of the New York Times is to try to find a way to spin it for their own political reasons to try to hurt President Trump!"
The Defense Secretary explained that the leaked report in question contained "low-confidence" information," meaning it is unclear how accurate any of it is. "If you want to make an assessment of **[what happened at Fordow, you better get a big shovel!" ](https://substack.com/redirect/6b4f8c66-a3bc-49f1-b806-f02afdb9579f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**Hegseth added.
Watch the explosive moment here:
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/6b4f8c66-a3bc-49f1-b806-f02afdb9579f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

# **[Trump's Push For America First](https://substack.com/redirect/ddd64af7-6f5b-44cd-8866-ed6f2ec0874a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

President Trump has been pushing the limits on what is possible. I haven't seen anything like this since President Ronald Reagan.

Yours Truly,
**SEAN HANNITY**

Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard confirmed that **["new intelligence" has verified the complete destruction](https://substack.com/redirect/62581f79-ed8e-43e4-b830-6d2c67db7f03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of Iran's key nuclear facilities at Natanz, Fordow, and Isfahan during last weekend's bombing campaign, stating that if Iran chose to rebuild, "they would have to rebuild all three facilities...entirely," which would "likely take years to do."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/62581f79-ed8e-43e4-b830-6d2c67db7f03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* * *
# Trump confirms US would strike Iran again if needed
President Donald Trump confirmed to reporters Wednesday that he is willing **[to strike Iran again](https://substack.com/redirect/66cef88b-c0b6-4cc5-a220-537a4b1271c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** if the country were to start to rebuild its nuclear program.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/66cef88b-c0b6-4cc5-a220-537a4b1271c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **The president says recent U.S. strikes on three Iranian sites "obliterated" the program**, crediting a report from Israel and asserting they set Iran's nuclear efforts back "many years."
* **Trump received praise by NATO Secretary General** Mark Rutte about his Iran decisiveness. "The fact that you are now also successful in getting this ceasefire done between Israel and Iran -- I really want to commend you for that," Rutte said. "I think this is important for the whole world."

* * *
# Homan: ICE saved "thousands" of migrant children trafficked over border
Trump Border Czar Tom Homan told the NY Post that **[ICE has rescued"thousands" of migrant children](https://substack.com/redirect/1a6bb16f-7860-4c58-a758-9f5c53f0a640?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** who went missing while being smuggled across the southern border.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1a6bb16f-7860-4c58-a758-9f5c53f0a640?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Massive Rescue Operations:** "Thousands" of migrant children who disappeared after being smuggled across the border during the Biden administration have been rescued from sex trafficking, forced labor, and other exploitation. Homan reported that ICE recently found a 14-year-old pregnant girl living with adult men and discovered children enslaved on ranches and chicken farms instead of attending school.
* **Staggering Numbers Missing:** The Biden administration lost track of 300,000 unaccompanied migrant children out of more than 500,000 who entered the country, with a DHS Inspector General report finding that over 31,000 sponsor addresses were "blank, undeliverable, or missing apartment numbers." In one area, sponsor addresses were incorrect 80% of the time, and thousands of children were released to non-family members.
* **Dangerous Placement Conditions:** Children were placed in potentially unsafe situations, including releases to unrelated sponsors or distant relatives, with three children released to "spouses" including one who was 40 years old. Inspector General visits found children in gang-controlled areas with "bars on the inside of windows," rundown apartments with no doors, dilapidated motels without kitchens, and locations where drug deals, stabbings and shootings occurred regularly.

body:
You don’t get over losing your health care. You don’t get over it when you lose someone you love because they couldn’t get the care they needed.
#

Peter, Republicans in the Senate are forcing through a budget that cuts health care for millions of people so they can give billionaires a tax cut.
They’re doing it in the face of near universal opposition. And they’re trying to tie all of their culture war and authoritarian ambitions into that budget, too.
“Failure is not an option.” That’s how Mitch McConnell described this budget. The Republican Party must not fail in its crusade to strip health care from the people who need it most, and give a massive tax break to the richest people in the world. He also said, “they’ll get over it.”
There’s a reason we’re fighting so hard against this, and it’s not hard to understand. Cutting health care for millions of people leaves them with no options. They get sick, they get sicker, and in the worst cases, they die.
I grew up poor. I know what it’s like to do without. And I can tell you something: You don’t get over losing your health care. You don’t get over it when you lose someone you love because they couldn’t get the care they needed.
Trump won on a platform of bringing down costs and making life affordable again. I’m all for it — and I have reached out to the White House to try and point them in the right direction. I’ve never heard back.
What the people who voted for Trump are getting is higher prices, a dollar that’s lost nearly 10% of its value over the last 6 months, and cuts to all the programs they depend on.
He’s failed. And instead of admitting it, accepting it, and working to turn things around, he’s digging us further and further into that hole. It will take decades to recover from this if we don’t stop them now.
I’m working around the clock to raise this alarm, stop this disaster of a budget, and hold these radical MAGA Republicans to account for what they’re trying to do. And if you’re willing, I’m asking you to help support that work.
[**Please, make a grassroots donation and help me keep going. We have to fight harder than ever now.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-june25.8rdpPa&refcode=em250625-1-90&t=1&akid=3901%2E734936%2EDTQzSt)
[DONATE](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-june25.8rdpPa&refcode=em250625-1-90&t=2&akid=3901%2E734936%2EDTQzSt)
Thank you,
Ruben

Friend, New York City voters just voted overwhelmingly for Zohran Mamdani, who ran on a bold agenda to make NYC more affordable for families struggling right now in the city. What makes it even more special is that Zohran is an unapologetic pro-Palestine democratic socialist. He won yesterday’s Democratic primary election against a billionaire-funded defender of the genocide in Gaza and the fascist Trump administration. This victory belongs to all of us and shows that when a candidate has the courage to take on the political establishment and fight for justice for everyday people, we can defeat the billionaire and corporate interests that too often control our politics. **We’re not stopping with Zohran’s win. This week, absentee ballots are getting sent to my district for local elections.** And my long-time colleague and comrade Denzel McCampbell is busy knocking on doors and talking to constituents in his race for Detroit City Council. Denzel is also a member of the LGBTQ+ community, and I was honored to march alongside him at this month’s Motor City Pride (he’s in the middle): [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsXu0R1XDWRVJnEMC9_ePsJYfTCgoXxVCxzBQjtX2I3-15AhkFYbwAaWuntpUSSI4Qk1tKHHB2Q4kCjwdv0if7sv87HGF82hAhRqll2Jojw4eLaCS3-bTb4fUXFocIKmh3zJR6WcQmUObzGL6XXLlZRuUhdS5VinSX8RMr0vlGnRfPIQ1KsqTkYhRASXoZ7UGsUJfa0to7WdasZ2u75eRyn63TdNwqinvrMrbA7WM91dDADhyVR-vdqDYD1Wmmr5QxR-YREwi1j4qniAJkonSqN7PwVJgwMy-GWIlElWjNWhEUnaQRblvMjmT0Y9DT7vYWFpvLHtmDpi5KxjTtLwFSdfFLQbnblRW_f6ZLRFxchBjDO0HEz4pxH7xjVXhC1zLBvCHAFYaTlTMA12DBLFd59ELrff-hqv3pJ2vF5b12Qpw/4hn/O9MVaEy0RAqlHSre74a8XA/h1/h001.cTs9-stes3_mlFUhR1icX834XHzCT9UCD0Hx1PJpVNM) Like me, Denzel was born and raised in Detroit, is dedicated to public service, and believes that everyone should have safe, well-resourced, and thriving neighborhoods. As my former Communications and Political Director, **his partnership in introducing bold policies and strong constituent services programs has already changed thousands of people’s lives**. For over a decade, I’ve seen Denzel fight hard for equity and human rights—including the essential right to clean air and affordable drinking water. He helped found the Detroit Chapter of BYP100, where he led the fight against police brutality and mass incarceration. And as an elected Detroit City Charter Commissioner, Denzel led an effort to revise our city’s governing documents to center the needs of residents. Denzel is a member of the DSA Metro Detroit chapter. **He’s pushing for a government that engages with and works for**** _all_****people, not just the powerful and wealthy... and he needs our help.** [**As people are receiving their absentee ballots in the mail, will you chip in today to support Denzel McCampbell’s visionary campaign for equity and justice?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsXu0R1XDWRVJnEMC9_ePsJYfTCgoXxVCxzBQjtX2I3-15AhkFYbwAaWuntpUSSI4QUzoTflnUF5zTmnLhN4-qmxmvuHROYbDkD1xkhiIf5OItqEcwV6BS7Fyh8BFLjgIs8sB2DmaegjU5FltX8lWQ198IQ4kexUqXGwFpbuZlaQY46ojWkHRgIy2Py3_zjIS63OFY1mQ1MdaVNqxfuT6p9J4PPCeX7zlmMsyE9zUEW21DZk0PwcP3m-qqtb1GMiNePj3iY9_WFmLREcN_Hed9HmEjj8MHOc7JmJRl1T8PKC_YzFf7FEVjOB599rzXeGq9EAMiAagiVdDfAPqUM1id-QJjjXjrtQXD3gEwqX67PSqcyFQZlgtcPl30IOrPQp5Ef_EpMwk0GNfz0lUWJfIq9H5EyMkfWJTnbSkt-pNq8IQ/4hn/O9MVaEy0RAqlHSre74a8XA/h2/h001.k1mlJdRNdFhlCFPUm82QHsti_gCLXQFwfLPdTgSFyc4) | [CHIP IN NOW](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsXu0R1XDWRVJnEMC9_ePsJYfTCgoXxVCxzBQjtX2I3-15AhkFYbwAaWuntpUSSI4RnxXhnxnpw3OIC5erH2-WrJxla-nxdHTqUwyEqz_iv1Zff8k6k0hBJIiQx1zDsQULAYJKY1lCXq3EZjL_n4jmU4SqI6QZ8L-Rnypa00311sz6b_-FBeOYTt8T1QNlpV5nyt4yCWL6r6cdKOHKsIeYgTy6MJIQAsM_wlPrQf_LWZ5hq8iWAh1LC8NPAUcrtpViHVXPbLzZ15EdPmqHVHDLY-kNCR5BhL2kxuOKouwN0LPgEiSvCWCUgiX8M2QcfvXsTjk14NTeNpGMvphZINdxYv6ytlDeZM3FhOfToc112ndYAfD24vE_6aGNMBdp84Y4QYG6qsvst_Gjg9KG9f9Ev87moyJNhszjp1J4rQZWduA/4hn/O9MVaEy0RAqlHSre74a8XA/h3/h001.E1fZ7m3q1gsyfbEAzeu9KVrybhKiKLbncqcXFMR4RXs)

Denzel is committed to fighting for truly**affordable housing** , protections for homeowners and tenants, mental health and **violence prevention programs to improve public safety** , resources and opportunities for **young people and seniors** , reliable and affordable **public transit** , an **accountable government** , and the well-being of everyday Detroiters.
His opponents include a State Representative who single-handedly forced the Michigan legislature to end its session early—while we had a Democratic trifecta and while policies for water affordability, Black maternal health, and voting rights were awaiting a vote.

clean_body: My colleague and comrade is knocking on doors and talking to everyday residents of our city. | | | Friend, New York City voters just voted overwhelmingly for Zohran Mamdani, who ran on a bold agenda to make NYC more affordable for families struggling right now in the city. What makes it even more special is that Zohran is an unapologetic pro-Palestine democratic socialist. He won yesterday’s Democratic primary election against a billionaire-funded defender of the genocide in Gaza and the fascist Trump administration. This victory belongs to all of us and shows that when a candidate has the courage to take on the political establishment and fight for justice for everyday people, we can defeat the billionaire and corporate interests that too often control our politics. We’re not stopping with Zohran’s win. This week, absentee ballots are getting sent to my district for local elections. And my long-time colleague and comrade Denzel McCampbell is busy knocking on doors and talking to constituents in his race for Detroit City Council. Denzel is also a member of the LGBTQ+ community, and I was honored to march alongside him at this month’s Motor City Pride (he’s in the middle): Like me, Denzel was born and raised in Detroit, is dedicated to public service, and believes that everyone should have safe, well-resourced, and thriving neighborhoods. As my former Communications and Political Director, his partnership in introducing bold policies and strong constituent services programs has already changed thousands of people’s lives. For over a decade, I’ve seen Denzel fight hard for equity and human rights—including the essential right to clean air and affordable drinking water. He helped found the Detroit Chapter of BYP100, where he led the fight against police brutality and mass incarceration. And as an elected Detroit City Charter Commissioner, Denzel led an effort to revise our city’s governing documents to center the needs of residents. Denzel is a member of the DSA Metro Detroit chapter. He’s pushing for a government that engages with and works for allpeople, not just the powerful and wealthy... and he needs our help. | Thank you for supporting this incredible grassroots leader. It’s no surprise to me that he’s been endorsed by a wide coalition of progressive groups including unions, the Working Families Party, Michigan Liberation, and Michigan United Action.1 Denzel is committed to fighting for trulyaffordable housing , protections for homeowners and tenants, mental health and violence prevention programs to improve public safety , resources and opportunities for young people and seniors , reliable and affordable public transit , an accountable government , and the well-being of everyday Detroiters. His opponents include a State Representative who single-handedly forced the Michigan legislature to end its session early—while we had a Democratic trifecta and while policies for water affordability, Black maternal health, and voting rights were awaiting a vote. We need representatives in government who are rooted in their community and who understand how urgently people need change. Atlanta Voice: Georgia seeks another Supreme Court showdown over Voting Rights Act
Bad news for everyone, Team: The state of Georgia is seeking another Supreme Court showdown over the Voting Rights Act, asking a federal appeals court to interpret the 1965 law in a way that could make it much harder to prove minority votes have been illegally diluted.
Georgia is trying persuade the judges to make up a new, harder-to-prove standard that could hobble Voting Rights Act lawsuits, less than two years after the U.S. Supreme Court turned back a separate challenge from Alabama to the VRA.
From the AP: " A lawyer for the state asked a three-judge panel of the 11th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals in Atlanta to overturn a lower court that required lawmakers to draw more Black-majority electoral districts. Georgia’s Republican Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger argued in court filings that the Voting Rights Act is being misused to bolster Democratic election chances and that white voters prefer Republicans for nonracial reasons. "
Opponents of voting rights are hell-bent on dismantling the Voting Rights Act piece by piece and we can't let them. We have to fight in Georgia, Alabama, and beyond to protect our fundamental rights

subject: BREAKING: We have a GOP opponent
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Gillibrand for Senate
body:
Scott Brown just announced his campaign in New Hampshire.
It’s official: **Scott Brown just announced he’s running to flip New Hampshire’s Senate seat red.** If that name sounds familiar, it’s because he’s run for Senate — and lost — before. In Massachusetts. Then he ran here, hoping Granite Staters wouldn’t notice. But we did. Now he’s back, with support from the national Republican machine, trying to buy his way into the Senate again. It’s up to our grassroots team to stop him. [**_Split a $10 contribution now between my campaign and Kirsten Gillibrand and join the fight to beat Scott Brown._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110250808/553741908/2095256023?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2025.06.25_Pappas-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_45AC_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTkvMS83MjcyMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1YWYwOGQ3Mi0wOTUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_AspoTh6XN57FXptHuiZKKrcdkBATf-TltLIaovwnSk=) **This is a serious threat.** The GOP sees New Hampshire as one of their best chances to expand their Senate majority — and they’re counting on Scott Brown to help them do it. _But this seat doesn’t belong to Scott Brown._ It belongs to the people of New Hampshire. I was born and raised here. I’ve run a family business, represented our communities in Concord and in Congress, and delivered for the people who call this state home — from lowering prescription drug costs to defending reproductive freedom and our democracy. Scott Brown’s record is clear: ❌ He supports Trump’s MAGA agenda.
❌ He voted to defund Planned Parenthood.

If you miss the live event, we will also share the recording of the speech and press coverage afterwards.
Thanks for being on our team,
Team Slotkin

Dear Fellow American,

I am enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter.

It will only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our nation's future.

A movement is growing, led by progressives—but supported by many well-meaning Americans—to change the way we elect our president. In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution.

That's why Hillsdale College is conducting a National Survey on Presidential Selection.

By completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue—views we will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders.

You can complete the National Survey on Presidential Selection by using the link below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=17x64w94u6jj4mxn9ywli7mp2t7ureientejzcq3xd1y1d4zbultzgac81t0dmbyygbmp2wrtcmrkm9pmda0dfxuuy88zpid4v3u3039u7qnmflatonxnqzdn126ufvpz59qtuaqlccyriuapw1tseu01mertv&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=syfl2h&__onlt=t

Do you think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government?

YES

NO
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=syfl2h&__onlt=t

For most of our nation's history, the Electoral College, as devised by the Framers of our Constitution, was not controversial. Indeed, it was considered essential to preserving free and representative government.

But today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with a proper grounding in American civics—too many Americans simply don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states.

These efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online courses, such as "Constitution 101" and "The Great American Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including American civics) to thousands of American educators and homeschoolers.

Your answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty—including the importance of the Electoral College.

And this is especially important in this critical time for America's future.

So please share your views on this urgent topic by completing our National Survey on Presidential Selection and returning it to me as soon as possible. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

You can take the survey using this secure link I've provided below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=17x64w94u6jj4mxn9ywli7mp2t7ureienu2wc6xhvxfv96fg365g9bv0jl78qsi63ohfse10ie6p0y9icycay4jy8t1pd9vpq9eqhl07f7n25ag6tka1oikb0843ys6p9qknds58vn2i59n50viv6tlb4xc3jr&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=syfl2h&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=syfl2h&__onlt=t

And after you take your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Since 1844, Hillsdale has been "pursuing truth and defending liberty." Today, it does so through its extensive educational outreach efforts while refusing to accept ONE PENNY of government funding—not even indirectly in the form of federal or state student grants or loans.

The support of private citizens like you is essential to our work.

Please represent your state and take the National Survey on Presidential Selection today. Thank you for your time and attention—and for your friendship and support of liberty.

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn

President, Hillsdale College

Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

name: Scott Brown
subject: I have something personal to share with you
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scott Brown for New Hampshire, Inc
body:
Peter ,

My name is Scott Brown, and I want to take a few minutes to share my story
with you and how the experiences and lessons I’ve learned have led me to make a
big decision this week.
I had a challenging upbringing. My mom was married and divorced four times,
and my dad was married and divorced three times. I was raised by my single mom,
who worked multiple jobs to put food on the table. We didn’t have much, but
with the love and support of my grandparents, we had a fighting chance. We
moved often—I lived in 17 different places before I turned 18.

<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaey_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
I know what it’s like to worry about where your next meal is coming from or
whether the bills all get paid.And those early years taught me the value of
grit, of resilience, and hard work.

Nothing in my life has ever been handed to me — I’ve had to fight for every
step forward.

I worked my way through college and law school, taking any odd job and doing
whatever it took to stay afloat.

At 19, I joined the Army National Guard. I served for more than 30 years and
retired as a Colonel. I’ve worn our nation’s uniform with pride and know
firsthand what it means to serve a cause bigger than yourself.

<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaey_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
Back in 2010, I took a leap that many thought was crazy. I ran for the U.S.
Senate in Massachusetts as a Republican,driven by a belief that people like you
deserved a real voice in Washington, not just another career politician. I
drove across the state, putting countless miles on my beloved truck, a 2005 GMC
Canyon. With the incredible support of grassroots supporters like you from all
corners of the country,we pulled off a stunning upset and won, shaking the
political establishment to its core.

But that victory was just the start.

I went to Washington as a disruptor, refusing to play the insider games of
career politicians. That made me a target. The national Democrats zeroed in,
recruiting Elizabeth Warren and pouring tens of millions into a campaign to
defeat me. Despite our best efforts, we came up short in that race.

But I wasn’t discouraged. I believed then, and I believe now, that there’s a
bigger plan for all of us.

My wife, Gail, and I became four-time grandparents, and we’ve poured our
hearts into our family and our New Hampshire community. In 2017, when President
Trump asked me to serve as U.S. Ambassador to New Zealand and Samoa,I was
honored to represent our nation, strengthen global partnerships, and protect
American interests abroad.
<https://secure.winred.com/nrsc/doge-hit-ground-running-tc-rs-hf/?recurring=true&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&address=&zip=&city=&state=&employer_name=&occupation=&amtposition=4>

<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaey_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
Today, I’m writing to you with big news: I’m not done fighting. Our country’s
future is at a crossroads, and I’m stepping up again to run for the U.S. Senate
in New Hampshire.I’m doing this for you, for our shared values, and for the
America we believe in. Chip in to Join Scott Brown »
<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaey_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
You’ve seen what happens when Democrats hold unchecked power...

Runaway inflation...

Chaos at our southern border...

Soft-on-crime policies...

Men in women’s sports and locker rooms...

Foreign policy missteps that weaken our allies and embolden our enemies.

Hardworking Americans like you are being left behind, and we can’t let this
radical agenda take over the Senate in 2026.The stakes are just too high.

Here’s the truth: I can’t do this without you.

The Democrats and their elite allies will flood this race with MILLIONS. It’s
an open seat in a swing state. They don’t want someone like me—someone who
speaks plainly, serves with honor, and refuses to sell out—anywhere near
Washington.

That’s why I’m reaching out to you today, asking you to stand with me from
Day One.

A contribution of $5, $10, or whatever you can give will help us build a
campaign powered by people like you, not political insiders.
<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaey_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
Every dollar counts, and every voice matters. Chip in to Join Scott Brown »
<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaey_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
If you’ve ever felt like your voice doesn’t matter, I’m here to tell you it
does. It matters to me. And it’s the only reason I’m in this fight.

Let’s do this together.

Scott Brown
Candidate for U.S. Senate
New Hampshire Chip in to Join Scott Brown »
<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaey_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>

Years after Judicial Watch reported that the government’s
system to verify if employees are authorized to work legally in the
United States approved hundreds of thousands of illegal immigrants,
federal authorities have uncovered widespread identity theft at a meat
processing plant that used the defective tool to screen 100% of its
staff. A recent Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) worksite
enforcement operation at Glenn Valley Foods in Omaha, Nebraska busted
over 70 illegal aliens who were using stolen Social Security numbers
and identities to unlawfully obtain wages, health benefits and
employment authorization, according to the agency. The criminal
identity theft scheme left “more than 100 real victims to face
devastating financial, emotional and legal consequences,” ICE writes
in its announcement of the operation.

President Trump got another win at the NATO summit, as NATO allies pledge 5% annual increase in defense spending by 2035. NATO Chief Mark Rutte called President Trump "daddy" after he rebuked Israel and Iran for breaking the ceasefire. Despite the fake news' best efforts, Israeli intelligence has confirmed that the nuclear sites in Iran are in fact obliterated. The NYC Mayoral race just concluded with a Socialist, Communist, extreme radical Zohran Mamdani toppling Andrew Cuomo. The receipts are plentiful on where Mamdani stands on issues and Democrats now have to own this. Senator Ron Johnson is with me to discuss the big, beautiful bill. As an accountant Senator Johnson has a brand new report that addresses our deficit, annual growth and 10 year CBO projections. Sen. Johnson has been fighting to get government spending under control, preferably to pre-pandemic levels. He lays out different scenarios based on our current spending, growth and interest. Sen. Johnson is worried and frustrated by the overwhelming burden we are leaving the next generation.

* **TOP NEWS**

"**Former Ken Paxton aides allege witness tampering during impeachment trial,** " Austin American-Statesman's **Taylor Goldenstein** - "Several former and current top aides of Attorney General **Ken Paxton** are trading explosive accusations in legal and administrative filings, the latest of which alleges that Paxton's right-hand deputy obstructed justice and tampered with witnesses during his 2023 impeachment.

The public feud could become a distraction for Paxton just as he's overcome a series of legal troubles, including the impeachment charges, which he was [acquitted of by the Texas Senate](https://substack.com/redirect/ec164f9e-bbaf-4aeb-a4af-2a4be5aebc23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and as he launches his bid to unseat U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** in next year's Republican primary.

The new allegations -- detailed in a suit filed Wednesday in federal court in Austin by former Solicitor General **Judd Stone** and**Chris Hilton** , the former chief of the general litigation division -- include claims that current First Assistant Attorney General **Brent Webster** threatened to fire employees if they gave testimony during the impeachment proceedings that was unfavorable to Paxton. The claim has not previously been reported, and Webster did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/83c711e8-3434-4c63-9572-cd3c992f9675?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It's not clear if the claims were ever raised to law enforcement; Webster has not been charged with any criminal wrongdoing.

The first lawsuit was filed last month by **Jordan Eskew** , a former executive assistant for Stone and Hilton, against the two men and their private law firm. Eskew accused Stone of sexual harassment on multiple occasions in 2023 when she had taken leave from Paxton's office to work for Stone and Hilton as private attorneys representing Paxton in the impeachment trial. She also claimed Hilton failed to protect her and that the two created a hostile work environment.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/83c711e8-3434-4c63-9572-cd3c992f9675?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A spokesperson for Stone and Hilton's law firm has called Eskew's suit "a complete fabrication" and said that it was pushed by Paxton's top deputy, Webster, who has a "personal vendetta" against Stone and Hilton. Webster and Eskew are still working at the attorney general's office.

This week, Stone and Hilton shot back with a suit of their own against Webster and other attorney general staffers, not including Eskew, and a bar complaint against Webster _._

They claim Webster tried to damage their careers by lying about them and encouraging Eskew to file her sexual harassment suit.

Stone and Hilton also claimed in the filing to the State Bar of Texas that Webster tried to tamper with potential witnesses for Paxton's impeachment proceedings by pressuring them to give favorable testimony or "to flee the state to evade being subpoenaed to disclose information harmful to Webster." It does not specify which people were targeted.

Webster also demanded that Stone and Hilton "disclose confidential information" during the impeachment proceedings, which would have violated their professional obligation to Paxton, according to the bar complaint.

When they refused to share the information, the complaint alleges, Webster threatened retaliation against them and the firm.

The bar complaint also alleges Webster abused the power of his office by, in part, leveraging meetings with private citizens and lawyers to try to obtain future lucrative employment and harm his enemies.

The Bar's law office will now review the complaint and decide within the next 30 days whether the allegations amount to professional misconduct, and if so, it will conduct an investigation.

The harassment claims

Eskew's lawsuit claims Stone made a sexual comment and yelled at her several times at their law firm, and Hilton stood by and did nothing.

She alleges that Stone responded to her statement at a work lunch that a shot of alcohol was "the most disgusting thing I have ever tasted" by saying, "I highly doubt that is the most disgusting thing that has ever been in your mouth." Hilton, according to the complaint, did nothing but wince and laugh uncomfortably.

It also described a situation in which Stone and Hilton berated Eskew for taking too long to get a BBQ lunch to the staff and multiple other occasions in which Stone yelled at her and other female employees. It alleged Stone called her "white trash" because she was wearing turquoise earrings and that he asked her to buy alcohol and make drinks as part of her job duties.

One time, the suit alleges, Stone told her: "If anyone else makes a comment about my drinking, they'll be fired." Another time, he told her that at his firm, "you can say whatever slurs you want."

The Texas Workforce Commission previously determined that Eskew had grounds to bring a harassment suit, and in a filing to the TWC, Stone admitted to making the comments but "denied the sexual nature" of them, according to Eskew's suit.

Stone, Hilton and Eskew were among the lawyers who took leave from the attorney general's office in 2023 to represent Paxton during the impeachment. Eskew claims that upon their return, they were asked to resign after she raised concerns about their behavior during the impeachment period. They deny that they were forced to leave, and their suit suggests they left because of their differences with Webster. Stone and Hilton declined an interview request for this story.

Four other lawyers who returned to the attorney general's office after working at Stone and Hilton's private firm during the impeachment process have entered into paid settlement agreements that prohibit them from disparaging the firm owners, according to the suit, though it does not say when. They agreed to a statement saying the lawyers "parted ways professionally" and "amiably" with Stone and Hilton. Eskew refused to agree to the statement, according to the suit.

The Webster connection

Webster wasn't a plaintiff in Eskew's suit, but he indicated in an internal email cited in the complaint that two women who worked with Stone and Hilton told him they were afraid of potential assault or further harassment by the men.

Webster also wrote that he had heard from one of the women that Stone had openly fantasized about Webster being harmed and as a result, Webster feared for his and his family's safety.

Stone and Hilton denied Webster's account and all accusations of sexual harassment in Eskew's filing. They claim Webster was angry with them for pushing to get access to records after they left that they believed would expose wrongdoing.

"The email is nothing more than retaliation against Plaintiffs for their refusal to play ball with a corrupt public official," their suit reads. "Webster sent the email in response to Plaintiffs' efforts to obtain documents that would prove his corruption."

Eskew's lawsuit has caused Stone and Hilton "significant embarrassment and a loss of standing in their professional and personal circles -- just as Defendants intended," they write in their suit.

Days after Eskew's suit went public, Stone stepped down from the Federal Judicial Evaluation Committee, a panel of attorneys who screen judicial candidates for Texas' two senators, saying he did not want "the recent false and scurrilous accusations against me to overshadow the committee," [according to Bloomberg News](https://substack.com/redirect/be458e3f-2d95-4305-9fdb-96ce320a9eab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." [AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/622e2947-dafe-4fce-80d9-83456f2db963?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

"**ERCOT hustling to prepare Texas electric grid for record summer demand,** " San Antonio Express-News' **Sara DiNatale** - "Bracing for record-high demand this summer, the Texas grid operator is setting up temporary generators at San Antonio substations as part of [its plan](https://substack.com/redirect/750b3b00-7e1c-4624-af02-861b733c5e81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to prevent a statewide transmission meltdown.

The [Electric Reliability Council of Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/cd6fede8-3cab-4caf-99ff-f79919b86777?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) said its latest forecast calls for this summer's peak demand to reach 87.5 gigawatts -- 2 gigawatts higher than the current record.

[ERCOT](https://substack.com/redirect/cd6fede8-3cab-4caf-99ff-f79919b86777?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) President and CEO **Pablo Vegas** said the grid he oversees is ready to handle it.

"The state of the grid is strong," he told board members Tuesday. "It is as reliable as it has ever been, and it is as ready for the challenges of extreme weather that we have ever experienced. And so I feel confident that we are ready for this upcoming summer season."

While ERCOT anticipates the state's power plants will produce enough capacity to meet the demand, the state's sagging transmission infrastructure could pose challenges moving that power to where it's needed when it's needed. A problematic circuit that makes a loop around San Antonio could cause cascading outages across the state if overloaded.

That's why ERCOT is shelling out more than $110 million of its ratepayer-funded budget to tap a temporary generator fleet from Houston for about 450 megawatts and to keep an aging CPS Energy natural gas plant open past its prime -- adding another 400 megawatts of power in the troubled area.

The old plant won't be fixed up in time to operate this summer, but some of the generators will be ready to go in a couple weeks, Vegas announced.

It's part of ERCOT's plan to keep the lines from being overburdened, especially when plentiful power from South Texas wind farms and batteries is needed in North Texas, where generation capacity hasn't kept up with increasing demand. The location of the plant, Unit 3 at Braunig Power Station, means that ERCOT can use it -- along with the 15 generators, tied to nine key substations along the problematic circuit -- to reduce the number of electrons zipping across the troubled power lines at times of high demand.

CPS already is working on a long-term fix for the transmission challenges -- building out expanded power lines. At ERCOT's request, they've speeded up the timeline to get the line upgrades completed.

The temporary generator fleet has a contentious past. It was originally under the control of Houston electricity and natural gas provider CenterPoint Energy as part of an $800 million contract with owner LifeCyle Power. It was intended to provide backup power to keep Houston powered amid severe weather.

But when Hurricane Beryl tore through Houston, knocking out power for days, most of the generators were never deployed. That's because 15 of the 20 contracted machines take several days to assemble and need special permits -- not well suited for sudden outages caused by a storm, despite being billed as "mobile generators" by CenterPoint.

Five of the generators already have been moved to San Antonio and four were fully assembled as of Tuesday. A second set of five were expected to arrive Wednesday.

"What the contract provides for is bringing roughly five generators online into the San Antonio area every 31 days, with the first generators beginning operation by the early part of July," Vegas said.

Once they're assembled, the generators can be fired up quickly to provide emergency backup services to support the transmission infrastructure while permanent line upgrades are ongoing.

The fleet is contracted until March 31, 2027, but can exit San Antonio sooner if the transmission expansion finishes up sooner. The contracted cost, to be shared by ratepayers across Texas, is $54 million." TOP NEWS "Former Ken Paxton aides allege witness tampering during impeachment trial, " Austin American-Statesman's Taylor Goldenstein - "Several former and current top aides of Attorney General Ken Paxton are trading explosive accusations in legal and administrative filings, the latest of which alleges that Paxton's right-hand deputy obstructed justice and tampered with witnesses during his 2023 impeachment. The public feud could become a distraction for Paxton just as he's overcome a series of legal troubles, including the impeachment charges, which he was , and as he launches his bid to unseat U.S. Sen. John Cornyn in next year's Republican primary. The new allegations -- detailed in a suit filed Wednesday in federal court in Austin by former Solicitor General Judd Stone andChris Hilton , the former chief of the general litigation division -- include claims that current First Assistant Attorney General Brent Webster threatened to fire employees if they gave testimony during the impeachment proceedings that was unfavorable to Paxton. The claim has not previously been reported, and Webster did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It's not clear if the claims were ever raised to law enforcement; Webster has not been charged with any criminal wrongdoing. The first lawsuit was filed last month by Jordan Eskew , a former executive assistant for Stone and Hilton, against the two men and their private law firm. Eskew accused Stone of sexual harassment on multiple occasions in 2023 when she had taken leave from Paxton's office to work for Stone and Hilton as private attorneys representing Paxton in the impeachment trial. She also claimed Hilton failed to protect her and that the two created a hostile work environment. A spokesperson for Stone and Hilton's law firm has called Eskew's suit "a complete fabrication" and said that it was pushed by Paxton's top deputy, Webster, who has a "personal vendetta" against Stone and Hilton. Webster and Eskew are still working at the attorney general's office. This week, Stone and Hilton shot back with a suit of their own against Webster and other attorney general staffers, not including Eskew, and a bar complaint against Webster . They claim Webster tried to damage their careers by lying about them and encouraging Eskew to file her sexual harassment suit. Stone and Hilton also claimed in the filing to the State Bar of Texas that Webster tried to tamper with potential witnesses for Paxton's impeachment proceedings by pressuring them to give favorable testimony or "to flee the state to evade being subpoenaed to disclose information harmful to Webster." It does not specify which people were targeted. Webster also demanded that Stone and Hilton "disclose confidential information" during the impeachment proceedings, which would have violated their professional obligation to Paxton, according to the bar complaint. When they refused to share the information, the complaint alleges, Webster threatened retaliation against them and the firm. The bar complaint also alleges Webster abused the power of his office by, in part, leveraging meetings with private citizens and lawyers to try to obtain future lucrative employment and harm his enemies. The Bar's law office will now review the complaint and decide within the next 30 days whether the allegations amount to professional misconduct, and if so, it will conduct an investigation. The harassment claims Eskew's lawsuit claims Stone made a sexual comment and yelled at her several times at their law firm, and Hilton stood by and did nothing. She alleges that Stone responded to her statement at a work lunch that a shot of alcohol was "the most disgusting thing I have ever tasted" by saying, "I highly doubt that is the most disgusting thing that has ever been in your mouth." Hilton, according to the complaint, did nothing but wince and laugh uncomfortably. It also described a situation in which Stone and Hilton berated Eskew for taking too long to get a BBQ lunch to the staff and multiple other occasions in which Stone yelled at her and other female employees. It alleged Stone called her "white trash" because she was wearing turquoise earrings and that he asked her to buy alcohol and make drinks as part of her job duties. One time, the suit alleges, Stone told her: "If anyone else makes a comment about my drinking, they'll be fired." Another time, he told her that at his firm, "you can say whatever slurs you want." The Texas Workforce Commission previously determined that Eskew had grounds to bring a harassment suit, and in a filing to the TWC, Stone admitted to making the comments but "denied the sexual nature" of them, according to Eskew's suit. Stone, Hilton and Eskew were among the lawyers who took leave from the attorney general's office in 2023 to represent Paxton during the impeachment. Eskew claims that upon their return, they were asked to resign after she raised concerns about their behavior during the impeachment period. They deny that they were forced to leave, and their suit suggests they left because of their differences with Webster. Stone and Hilton declined an interview request for this story. Four other lawyers who returned to the attorney general's office after working at Stone and Hilton's private firm during the impeachment process have entered into paid settlement agreements that prohibit them from disparaging the firm owners, according to the suit, though it does not say when. They agreed to a statement saying the lawyers "parted ways professionally" and "amiably" with Stone and Hilton. Eskew refused to agree to the statement, according to the suit. The Webster connection Webster wasn't a plaintiff in Eskew's suit, but he indicated in an internal email cited in the complaint that two women who worked with Stone and Hilton told him they were afraid of potential assault or further harassment by the men. Webster also wrote that he had heard from one of the women that Stone had openly fantasized about Webster being harmed and as a result, Webster feared for his and his family's safety. Stone and Hilton denied Webster's account and all accusations of sexual harassment in Eskew's filing. They claim Webster was angry with them for pushing to get access to records after they left that they believed would expose wrongdoing. "The email is nothing more than retaliation against Plaintiffs for their refusal to play ball with a corrupt public official," their suit reads. "Webster sent the email in response to Plaintiffs' efforts to obtain documents that would prove his corruption." Eskew's lawsuit has caused Stone and Hilton "significant embarrassment and a loss of standing in their professional and personal circles -- just as Defendants intended," they write in their suit. Days after Eskew's suit went public, Stone stepped down from the Federal Judicial Evaluation Committee, a panel of attorneys who screen judicial candidates for Texas' two senators, saying he did not want "the recent false and scurrilous accusations against me to overshadow the committee," ." ($) "ERCOT hustling to prepare Texas electric grid for record summer demand, " San Antonio Express-News' Sara DiNatale - "Bracing for record-high demand this summer, the Texas grid operator is setting up temporary generators at San Antonio substations as part of to prevent a statewide transmission meltdown. The said its latest forecast calls for this summer's peak demand to reach 87.5 gigawatts -- 2 gigawatts higher than the current record. President and CEO Pablo Vegas said the grid he oversees is ready to handle it. "The state of the grid is strong," he told board members Tuesday. "It is as reliable as it has ever been, and it is as ready for the challenges of extreme weather that we have ever experienced. And so I feel confident that we are ready for this upcoming summer season." While ERCOT anticipates the state's power plants will produce enough capacity to meet the demand, the state's sagging transmission infrastructure could pose challenges moving that power to where it's needed when it's needed. A problematic circuit that makes a loop around San Antonio could cause cascading outages across the state if overloaded. That's why ERCOT is shelling out more than $110 million of its ratepayer-funded budget to tap a temporary generator fleet from Houston for about 450 megawatts and to keep an aging CPS Energy natural gas plant open past its prime -- adding another 400 megawatts of power in the troubled area. The old plant won't be fixed up in time to operate this summer, but some of the generators will be ready to go in a couple weeks, Vegas announced. It's part of ERCOT's plan to keep the lines from being overburdened, especially when plentiful power from South Texas wind farms and batteries is needed in North Texas, where generation capacity hasn't kept up with increasing demand. The location of the plant, Unit 3 at Braunig Power Station, means that ERCOT can use it -- along with the 15 generators, tied to nine key substations along the problematic circuit -- to reduce the number of electrons zipping across the troubled power lines at times of high demand. CPS already is working on a long-term fix for the transmission challenges -- building out expanded power lines. At ERCOT's request, they've speeded up the timeline to get the line upgrades completed. The temporary generator fleet has a contentious past. It was originally under the control of Houston electricity and natural gas provider CenterPoint Energy as part of an $800 million contract with owner LifeCyle Power. It was intended to provide backup power to keep Houston powered amid severe weather. But when Hurricane Beryl tore through Houston, knocking out power for days, most of the generators were never deployed. That's because 15 of the 20 contracted machines take several days to assemble and need special permits -- not well suited for sudden outages caused by a storm, despite being billed as "mobile generators" by CenterPoint. Five of the generators already have been moved to San Antonio and four were fully assembled as of Tuesday. A second set of five were expected to arrive Wednesday. "What the contract provides for is bringing roughly five generators online into the San Antonio area every 31 days, with the first generators beginning operation by the early part of July," Vegas said. Once they're assembled, the generators can be fired up quickly to provide emergency backup services to support the transmission infrastructure while permanent line upgrades are ongoing. The fleet is contracted until March 31, 2027, but can exit San Antonio sooner if the transmission expansion finishes up sooner. The contracted cost, to be shared by ratepayers across Texas, is $54 million." ($) FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. Hey Peter —
We wanted to make sure you saw Pete Buttigieg’s note about Jon Ossoff’s re-election campaign.
Like Pete said, there is no path to retaking the Senate majority that doesn’t run through Georgia.
So if you have a moment, read Pete’s full message below, and if you can, [**please make a contribution to Jon Ossoff’s re-election campaign today.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-june25.2OdyOr&refcode=em250625-1-full&t=1&akid=502%2E5691347%2EnOiX93)
