Peter — it’s Pete Buttigieg. We are living through a time in the life of our country when freedom itself is on the line — and few races will test that more directly than Jon Ossoff’s re-election campaign in Georgia. **I’ll share more in a moment. But if you believe, as I do, that hope can be the consequence of action, one meaningful step you can take today is to support Jon’s campaign using this link:** [**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ossoff-em-june25?refcode=Pete**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-june25.2OdyOr&refcode=em250625-1-full&t=3&akid=502%2E5691347%2EnOiX93) Right now, the same forces working to consolidate total power in Washington have made Jon their top Senate target. They’re prepared to spend whatever it takes to replace Jon with someone who will help them undermine the freedom of working people. They need to replace Jon with one more Senate enabler of this administration’s abuses of power. Let’s be clear about what that means. When the tools of government are used to make people more afraid, more angry, and more alone — it’s serving the opposite of the government’s true purpose. A well-run government enhances freedom — from fundamental freedoms like the right to speak your mind, to the economic freedoms that come from access to health care, and an affordable everyday life for your family. I don’t say this lightly, and I wouldn’t ask if it weren’t urgent. This is one of those moments that will define what comes next: for Jon’s campaign, for Georgia, and for our country. And it’s going to take all of us. [**That’s why I’m asking: Would you please join me in supporting Jon Ossoff’s re-election campaign by making a donation of any amount today?**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-june25.2OdyOr&refcode=em250625-1-full&t=4&akid=502%2E5691347%2EnOiX93) Gratefully, — Pete

* **TOP NEWS**

"**Former Ken Paxton aides allege witness tampering during impeachment trial,** " Austin American-Statesman's **Taylor Goldenstein** - "Several former and current top aides of Attorney General **Ken Paxton** are trading explosive accusations in legal and administrative filings, the latest of which alleges that Paxton's right-hand deputy obstructed justice and tampered with witnesses during his 2023 impeachment.

The public feud could become a distraction for Paxton just as he's overcome a series of legal troubles, including the impeachment charges, which he was [acquitted of by the Texas Senate](https://substack.com/redirect/592452f8-fe80-420b-a279-4ab0d4c17648?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and as he launches his bid to unseat U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** in next year's Republican primary.

The new allegations -- detailed in a suit filed Wednesday in federal court in Austin by former Solicitor General **Judd Stone** and**Chris Hilton** , the former chief of the general litigation division -- include claims that current First Assistant Attorney General **Brent Webster** threatened to fire employees if they gave testimony during the impeachment proceedings that was unfavorable to Paxton. The claim has not previously been reported, and Webster did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/e9611491-04fb-4ed5-8b4c-2e870a5d982a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It's not clear if the claims were ever raised to law enforcement; Webster has not been charged with any criminal wrongdoing.

The first lawsuit was filed last month by **Jordan Eskew** , a former executive assistant for Stone and Hilton, against the two men and their private law firm. Eskew accused Stone of sexual harassment on multiple occasions in 2023 when she had taken leave from Paxton's office to work for Stone and Hilton as private attorneys representing Paxton in the impeachment trial. She also claimed Hilton failed to protect her and that the two created a hostile work environment.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/e9611491-04fb-4ed5-8b4c-2e870a5d982a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A spokesperson for Stone and Hilton's law firm has called Eskew's suit "a complete fabrication" and said that it was pushed by Paxton's top deputy, Webster, who has a "personal vendetta" against Stone and Hilton. Webster and Eskew are still working at the attorney general's office.

This week, Stone and Hilton shot back with a suit of their own against Webster and other attorney general staffers, not including Eskew, and a bar complaint against Webster _._

They claim Webster tried to damage their careers by lying about them and encouraging Eskew to file her sexual harassment suit.

Stone and Hilton also claimed in the filing to the State Bar of Texas that Webster tried to tamper with potential witnesses for Paxton's impeachment proceedings by pressuring them to give favorable testimony or "to flee the state to evade being subpoenaed to disclose information harmful to Webster." It does not specify which people were targeted.

Webster also demanded that Stone and Hilton "disclose confidential information" during the impeachment proceedings, which would have violated their professional obligation to Paxton, according to the bar complaint.

When they refused to share the information, the complaint alleges, Webster threatened retaliation against them and the firm.

The bar complaint also alleges Webster abused the power of his office by, in part, leveraging meetings with private citizens and lawyers to try to obtain future lucrative employment and harm his enemies.

The Bar's law office will now review the complaint and decide within the next 30 days whether the allegations amount to professional misconduct, and if so, it will conduct an investigation.

The harassment claims

Eskew's lawsuit claims Stone made a sexual comment and yelled at her several times at their law firm, and Hilton stood by and did nothing.

She alleges that Stone responded to her statement at a work lunch that a shot of alcohol was "the most disgusting thing I have ever tasted" by saying, "I highly doubt that is the most disgusting thing that has ever been in your mouth." Hilton, according to the complaint, did nothing but wince and laugh uncomfortably.

It also described a situation in which Stone and Hilton berated Eskew for taking too long to get a BBQ lunch to the staff and multiple other occasions in which Stone yelled at her and other female employees. It alleged Stone called her "white trash" because she was wearing turquoise earrings and that he asked her to buy alcohol and make drinks as part of her job duties.

One time, the suit alleges, Stone told her: "If anyone else makes a comment about my drinking, they'll be fired." Another time, he told her that at his firm, "you can say whatever slurs you want."

The Texas Workforce Commission previously determined that Eskew had grounds to bring a harassment suit, and in a filing to the TWC, Stone admitted to making the comments but "denied the sexual nature" of them, according to Eskew's suit.

Stone, Hilton and Eskew were among the lawyers who took leave from the attorney general's office in 2023 to represent Paxton during the impeachment. Eskew claims that upon their return, they were asked to resign after she raised concerns about their behavior during the impeachment period. They deny that they were forced to leave, and their suit suggests they left because of their differences with Webster. Stone and Hilton declined an interview request for this story.

Four other lawyers who returned to the attorney general's office after working at Stone and Hilton's private firm during the impeachment process have entered into paid settlement agreements that prohibit them from disparaging the firm owners, according to the suit, though it does not say when. They agreed to a statement saying the lawyers "parted ways professionally" and "amiably" with Stone and Hilton. Eskew refused to agree to the statement, according to the suit.

The Webster connection

Webster wasn't a plaintiff in Eskew's suit, but he indicated in an internal email cited in the complaint that two women who worked with Stone and Hilton told him they were afraid of potential assault or further harassment by the men.

Webster also wrote that he had heard from one of the women that Stone had openly fantasized about Webster being harmed and as a result, Webster feared for his and his family's safety.

Stone and Hilton denied Webster's account and all accusations of sexual harassment in Eskew's filing. They claim Webster was angry with them for pushing to get access to records after they left that they believed would expose wrongdoing.

"The email is nothing more than retaliation against Plaintiffs for their refusal to play ball with a corrupt public official," their suit reads. "Webster sent the email in response to Plaintiffs' efforts to obtain documents that would prove his corruption."

Eskew's lawsuit has caused Stone and Hilton "significant embarrassment and a loss of standing in their professional and personal circles -- just as Defendants intended," they write in their suit.

Days after Eskew's suit went public, Stone stepped down from the Federal Judicial Evaluation Committee, a panel of attorneys who screen judicial candidates for Texas' two senators, saying he did not want "the recent false and scurrilous accusations against me to overshadow the committee," [according to Bloomberg News](https://substack.com/redirect/ace1a510-c72a-4640-81df-2b8db206aad4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." [AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/7520d119-43e2-44d4-b9ad-feb23f4b87ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

"**ERCOT hustling to prepare Texas electric grid for record summer demand,** " San Antonio Express-News' **Sara DiNatale** - "Bracing for record-high demand this summer, the Texas grid operator is setting up temporary generators at San Antonio substations as part of [its plan](https://substack.com/redirect/cee09694-2e16-4392-afdb-c2efd3a724d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to prevent a statewide transmission meltdown.

The [Electric Reliability Council of Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/7bda9ae4-8752-40e0-a450-0d7b150ab371?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) said its latest forecast calls for this summer's peak demand to reach 87.5 gigawatts -- 2 gigawatts higher than the current record.

[ERCOT](https://substack.com/redirect/7bda9ae4-8752-40e0-a450-0d7b150ab371?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) President and CEO **Pablo Vegas** said the grid he oversees is ready to handle it.

"The state of the grid is strong," he told board members Tuesday. "It is as reliable as it has ever been, and it is as ready for the challenges of extreme weather that we have ever experienced. And so I feel confident that we are ready for this upcoming summer season."

While ERCOT anticipates the state's power plants will produce enough capacity to meet the demand, the state's sagging transmission infrastructure could pose challenges moving that power to where it's needed when it's needed. A problematic circuit that makes a loop around San Antonio could cause cascading outages across the state if overloaded.

That's why ERCOT is shelling out more than $110 million of its ratepayer-funded budget to tap a temporary generator fleet from Houston for about 450 megawatts and to keep an aging CPS Energy natural gas plant open past its prime -- adding another 400 megawatts of power in the troubled area.

The old plant won't be fixed up in time to operate this summer, but some of the generators will be ready to go in a couple weeks, Vegas announced.

It's part of ERCOT's plan to keep the lines from being overburdened, especially when plentiful power from South Texas wind farms and batteries is needed in North Texas, where generation capacity hasn't kept up with increasing demand. The location of the plant, Unit 3 at Braunig Power Station, means that ERCOT can use it -- along with the 15 generators, tied to nine key substations along the problematic circuit -- to reduce the number of electrons zipping across the troubled power lines at times of high demand.

CPS already is working on a long-term fix for the transmission challenges -- building out expanded power lines. At ERCOT's request, they've speeded up the timeline to get the line upgrades completed.

The temporary generator fleet has a contentious past. It was originally under the control of Houston electricity and natural gas provider CenterPoint Energy as part of an $800 million contract with owner LifeCyle Power. It was intended to provide backup power to keep Houston powered amid severe weather.

But when Hurricane Beryl tore through Houston, knocking out power for days, most of the generators were never deployed. That's because 15 of the 20 contracted machines take several days to assemble and need special permits -- not well suited for sudden outages caused by a storm, despite being billed as "mobile generators" by CenterPoint.

Five of the generators already have been moved to San Antonio and four were fully assembled as of Tuesday. A second set of five were expected to arrive Wednesday.

"What the contract provides for is bringing roughly five generators online into the San Antonio area every 31 days, with the first generators beginning operation by the early part of July," Vegas said.

Once they're assembled, the generators can be fired up quickly to provide emergency backup services to support the transmission infrastructure while permanent line upgrades are ongoing.

The fleet is contracted until March 31, 2027, but can exit San Antonio sooner if the transmission expansion finishes up sooner. The contracted cost, to be shared by ratepayers across Texas, is $54 million." TOP NEWS "Former Ken Paxton aides allege witness tampering during impeachment trial, " Austin American-Statesman's Taylor Goldenstein - "Several former and current top aides of Attorney General Ken Paxton are trading explosive accusations in legal and administrative filings, the latest of which alleges that Paxton's right-hand deputy obstructed justice and tampered with witnesses during his 2023 impeachment. The public feud could become a distraction for Paxton just as he's overcome a series of legal troubles, including the impeachment charges, which he was , and as he launches his bid to unseat U.S. Sen. John Cornyn in next year's Republican primary. The new allegations -- detailed in a suit filed Wednesday in federal court in Austin by former Solicitor General Judd Stone andChris Hilton , the former chief of the general litigation division -- include claims that current First Assistant Attorney General Brent Webster threatened to fire employees if they gave testimony during the impeachment proceedings that was unfavorable to Paxton. The claim has not previously been reported, and Webster did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It's not clear if the claims were ever raised to law enforcement; Webster has not been charged with any criminal wrongdoing. The first lawsuit was filed last month by Jordan Eskew , a former executive assistant for Stone and Hilton, against the two men and their private law firm. Eskew accused Stone of sexual harassment on multiple occasions in 2023 when she had taken leave from Paxton's office to work for Stone and Hilton as private attorneys representing Paxton in the impeachment trial. She also claimed Hilton failed to protect her and that the two created a hostile work environment. A spokesperson for Stone and Hilton's law firm has called Eskew's suit "a complete fabrication" and said that it was pushed by Paxton's top deputy, Webster, who has a "personal vendetta" against Stone and Hilton. Webster and Eskew are still working at the attorney general's office. This week, Stone and Hilton shot back with a suit of their own against Webster and other attorney general staffers, not including Eskew, and a bar complaint against Webster . They claim Webster tried to damage their careers by lying about them and encouraging Eskew to file her sexual harassment suit. Stone and Hilton also claimed in the filing to the State Bar of Texas that Webster tried to tamper with potential witnesses for Paxton's impeachment proceedings by pressuring them to give favorable testimony or "to flee the state to evade being subpoenaed to disclose information harmful to Webster." It does not specify which people were targeted. Webster also demanded that Stone and Hilton "disclose confidential information" during the impeachment proceedings, which would have violated their professional obligation to Paxton, according to the bar complaint. When they refused to share the information, the complaint alleges, Webster threatened retaliation against them and the firm. The bar complaint also alleges Webster abused the power of his office by, in part, leveraging meetings with private citizens and lawyers to try to obtain future lucrative employment and harm his enemies. The Bar's law office will now review the complaint and decide within the next 30 days whether the allegations amount to professional misconduct, and if so, it will conduct an investigation. The harassment claims Eskew's lawsuit claims Stone made a sexual comment and yelled at her several times at their law firm, and Hilton stood by and did nothing. She alleges that Stone responded to her statement at a work lunch that a shot of alcohol was "the most disgusting thing I have ever tasted" by saying, "I highly doubt that is the most disgusting thing that has ever been in your mouth." Hilton, according to the complaint, did nothing but wince and laugh uncomfortably. It also described a situation in which Stone and Hilton berated Eskew for taking too long to get a BBQ lunch to the staff and multiple other occasions in which Stone yelled at her and other female employees. It alleged Stone called her "white trash" because she was wearing turquoise earrings and that he asked her to buy alcohol and make drinks as part of her job duties. One time, the suit alleges, Stone told her: "If anyone else makes a comment about my drinking, they'll be fired." Another time, he told her that at his firm, "you can say whatever slurs you want." The Texas Workforce Commission previously determined that Eskew had grounds to bring a harassment suit, and in a filing to the TWC, Stone admitted to making the comments but "denied the sexual nature" of them, according to Eskew's suit. Stone, Hilton and Eskew were among the lawyers who took leave from the attorney general's office in 2023 to represent Paxton during the impeachment. Eskew claims that upon their return, they were asked to resign after she raised concerns about their behavior during the impeachment period. They deny that they were forced to leave, and their suit suggests they left because of their differences with Webster. Stone and Hilton declined an interview request for this story. Four other lawyers who returned to the attorney general's office after working at Stone and Hilton's private firm during the impeachment process have entered into paid settlement agreements that prohibit them from disparaging the firm owners, according to the suit, though it does not say when. They agreed to a statement saying the lawyers "parted ways professionally" and "amiably" with Stone and Hilton. Eskew refused to agree to the statement, according to the suit. The Webster connection Webster wasn't a plaintiff in Eskew's suit, but he indicated in an internal email cited in the complaint that two women who worked with Stone and Hilton told him they were afraid of potential assault or further harassment by the men. Webster also wrote that he had heard from one of the women that Stone had openly fantasized about Webster being harmed and as a result, Webster feared for his and his family's safety. Stone and Hilton denied Webster's account and all accusations of sexual harassment in Eskew's filing. They claim Webster was angry with them for pushing to get access to records after they left that they believed would expose wrongdoing. "The email is nothing more than retaliation against Plaintiffs for their refusal to play ball with a corrupt public official," their suit reads. "Webster sent the email in response to Plaintiffs' efforts to obtain documents that would prove his corruption." Eskew's lawsuit has caused Stone and Hilton "significant embarrassment and a loss of standing in their professional and personal circles -- just as Defendants intended," they write in their suit. Days after Eskew's suit went public, Stone stepped down from the Federal Judicial Evaluation Committee, a panel of attorneys who screen judicial candidates for Texas' two senators, saying he did not want "the recent false and scurrilous accusations against me to overshadow the committee," ." ($) "ERCOT hustling to prepare Texas electric grid for record summer demand, " San Antonio Express-News' Sara DiNatale - "Bracing for record-high demand this summer, the Texas grid operator is setting up temporary generators at San Antonio substations as part of to prevent a statewide transmission meltdown. The said its latest forecast calls for this summer's peak demand to reach 87.5 gigawatts -- 2 gigawatts higher than the current record. President and CEO Pablo Vegas said the grid he oversees is ready to handle it. "The state of the grid is strong," he told board members Tuesday. "It is as reliable as it has ever been, and it is as ready for the challenges of extreme weather that we have ever experienced. And so I feel confident that we are ready for this upcoming summer season." While ERCOT anticipates the state's power plants will produce enough capacity to meet the demand, the state's sagging transmission infrastructure could pose challenges moving that power to where it's needed when it's needed. A problematic circuit that makes a loop around San Antonio could cause cascading outages across the state if overloaded. That's why ERCOT is shelling out more than $110 million of its ratepayer-funded budget to tap a temporary generator fleet from Houston for about 450 megawatts and to keep an aging CPS Energy natural gas plant open past its prime -- adding another 400 megawatts of power in the troubled area. The old plant won't be fixed up in time to operate this summer, but some of the generators will be ready to go in a couple weeks, Vegas announced. It's part of ERCOT's plan to keep the lines from being overburdened, especially when plentiful power from South Texas wind farms and batteries is needed in North Texas, where generation capacity hasn't kept up with increasing demand. The location of the plant, Unit 3 at Braunig Power Station, means that ERCOT can use it -- along with the 15 generators, tied to nine key substations along the problematic circuit -- to reduce the number of electrons zipping across the troubled power lines at times of high demand. CPS already is working on a long-term fix for the transmission challenges -- building out expanded power lines. At ERCOT's request, they've speeded up the timeline to get the line upgrades completed. The temporary generator fleet has a contentious past. It was originally under the control of Houston electricity and natural gas provider CenterPoint Energy as part of an $800 million contract with owner LifeCyle Power. It was intended to provide backup power to keep Houston powered amid severe weather. But when Hurricane Beryl tore through Houston, knocking out power for days, most of the generators were never deployed. That's because 15 of the 20 contracted machines take several days to assemble and need special permits -- not well suited for sudden outages caused by a storm, despite being billed as "mobile generators" by CenterPoint. Five of the generators already have been moved to San Antonio and four were fully assembled as of Tuesday. A second set of five were expected to arrive Wednesday. "What the contract provides for is bringing roughly five generators online into the San Antonio area every 31 days, with the first generators beginning operation by the early part of July," Vegas said. Once they're assembled, the generators can be fired up quickly to provide emergency backup services to support the transmission infrastructure while permanent line upgrades are ongoing. The fleet is contracted until March 31, 2027, but can exit San Antonio sooner if the transmission expansion finishes up sooner. The contracted cost, to be shared by ratepayers across Texas, is $54 million." ($) FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. A spokesperson for Stone and Hilton’s law firm has called Eskew’s suit “a complete fabrication” and said that it was pushed by Paxton’s top deputy, Webster, who has a “personal vendetta” against Stone and Hilton. Webster and Eskew are still working at the attorney general’s office.

This week, Stone and Hilton shot back with a suit of their own against Webster and other attorney general staffers, not including Eskew, and a bar complaint against Webster _._

They claim Webster tried to damage their careers by lying about them and encouraging Eskew to file her sexual harassment suit.

Stone and Hilton also claimed in the filing to the State Bar of Texas that Webster tried to tamper with potential witnesses for Paxton’s impeachment proceedings by pressuring them to give favorable testimony or “to flee the state to evade being subpoenaed to disclose information harmful to Webster.” It does not specify which people were targeted.

Webster also demanded that Stone and Hilton “disclose confidential information” during the impeachment proceedings, which would have violated their professional obligation to Paxton, according to the bar complaint.

When they refused to share the information, the complaint alleges, Webster threatened retaliation against them and the firm.

The bar complaint also alleges Webster abused the power of his office by, in part, leveraging meetings with private citizens and lawyers to try to obtain future lucrative employment and harm his enemies.

The Bar’s law office will now review the complaint and decide within the next 30 days whether the allegations amount to professional misconduct, and if so, it will conduct an investigation.

The harassment claims

Eskew’s lawsuit claims Stone made a sexual comment and yelled at her several times at their law firm, and Hilton stood by and did nothing.

She alleges that Stone responded to her statement at a work lunch that a shot of alcohol was “the most disgusting thing I have ever tasted” by saying, “I highly doubt that is the most disgusting thing that has ever been in your mouth.” Hilton, according to the complaint, did nothing but wince and laugh uncomfortably.

It also described a situation in which Stone and Hilton berated Eskew for taking too long to get a BBQ lunch to the staff and multiple other occasions in which Stone yelled at her and other female employees. It alleged Stone called her “white trash” because she was wearing turquoise earrings and that he asked her to buy alcohol and make drinks as part of her job duties.

One time, the suit alleges, Stone told her: “If anyone else makes a comment about my drinking, they’ll be fired.” Another time, he told her that at his firm, “you can say whatever slurs you want.”

The Texas Workforce Commission previously determined that Eskew had grounds to bring a harassment suit, and in a filing to the TWC, Stone admitted to making the comments but “denied the sexual nature” of them, according to Eskew’s suit.

Stone, Hilton and Eskew were among the lawyers who took leave from the attorney general’s office in 2023 to represent Paxton during the impeachment. Eskew claims that upon their return, they were asked to resign after she raised concerns about their behavior during the impeachment period. They deny that they were forced to leave, and their suit suggests they left because of their differences with Webster. Stone and Hilton declined an interview request for this story.

Four other lawyers who returned to the attorney general’s office after working at Stone and Hilton’s private firm during the impeachment process have entered into paid settlement agreements that prohibit them from disparaging the firm owners, according to the suit, though it does not say when. They agreed to a statement saying the lawyers “parted ways professionally” and “amiably” with Stone and Hilton. Eskew refused to agree to the statement, according to the suit.

The Webster connection

Webster wasn’t a plaintiff in Eskew’s suit, but he indicated in an internal email cited in the complaint that two women who worked with Stone and Hilton told him they were afraid of potential assault or further harassment by the men.

Webster also wrote that he had heard from one of the women that Stone had openly fantasized about Webster being harmed and as a result, Webster feared for his and his family’s safety.

Stone and Hilton denied Webster’s account and all accusations of sexual harassment in Eskew’s filing. They claim Webster was angry with them for pushing to get access to records after they left that they believed would expose wrongdoing.

“The email is nothing more than retaliation against Plaintiffs for their refusal to play ball with a corrupt public official,” their suit reads. “Webster sent the email in response to Plaintiffs’ efforts to obtain documents that would prove his corruption.”

Eskew’s lawsuit has caused Stone and Hilton “significant embarrassment and a loss of standing in their professional and personal circles — just as Defendants intended,” they write in their suit.

“**ERCOT hustling to prepare Texas electric grid for record summer demand,** ” San Antonio Express-News' **Sara DiNatale** – “Bracing for record-high demand this summer, the Texas grid operator is setting up temporary generators at San Antonio substations as part of [its plan](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eLA4v3xJ7EFyLSWgpDk4sY8ZxH9AT_caGIyjyacIkJhS-QVWYSSnEaw1i0j2JuFBA3kVoofVajT9KZVusialv1yRqj7qeJbFzf0zmpJpVD_z7mGvfMaTwlqAo64xN8ZFAmAM002d9h74p-tonYtOWQg9X565eZv2SOBBesszwJCplqjXTSp0G_GOwTaW3ko1HEu7LsiGTJzG3vHUHj0ScOdlO9W2hhalnjA98cC0KTSvMiLKU0IV8hzhHDqK--Fzvm8TyweRNZbC7Qa5OnF4xhEsGpLPiBDLGg7ZVKJfJgD6zfUCVsfLQER7XvyTGFv7tZ5ohEKxh6xmOxumO_B7zSecHlAV10RViKrsVfqXxpayq7dBBvN6Ir-c_fvP7QDA2LQrnMfZj1Ml9dJT6lU5lyKkqlKVyvgb1fKolm2dSYTJNZElEtwanPYBqRbQz7FJf7d9teoocnbG1RG1caHz8gArBqLexQeYpjyiI2HZUajl4S9bz8MIAc20lZCoEjakCOuH3Q6KeYqtoIBwC2hBf8w/4hn/NabMlHgBQi6S-R2Kzsv5IA/h19/h001.DFwtIlxFg1-8GZB6iylMhAX4j2CVQSrKqvlq9w1HtDE) to prevent a statewide transmission meltdown.

The [Electric Reliability Council of Texas](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eND0tL88BVHcxBeP7dj5mAYIoWUhViIVawFybCcazduJIcm2OkMsR5M2xsQQFgMmg3BXC0iOQ1SO_x7bZuzG2EQqpyxrKV8983uMSm14arnBoIza9TIBmvaPWPd9W8pMoXESJdAkqAYsdfDZ58OZmnHEfwlJ-plxmvxpbrf3mpMYljsqzMK3xn3sxCoK-ppaZW7ClTg39sjflAZg9t4-n9Ufo96sirSG8rRuH4kYxiazdMem-RC0CWiq3YXU_3cCYagx2lwbVHgWvBvRRzqVvUNCeDyU265fmyMpABTjlH3-Nhm2HcY7gCbvRiaWI4awSKFfFMOx3F4nTK5ecdaB9xGYBKdg8H3Mp-6qQycNAo3lD022NBk0zCPz0oFGvlM56HCozgL-ErC53TJZjW9--TeABqqVKYfmoT6aI_2mA_tF/4hn/NabMlHgBQi6S-R2Kzsv5IA/h20/h001.Jx3cNnZbqwxmRyzgTSn4RKOc9GfDZuk8y4niU5J2IN8) said its latest forecast calls for this summer’s peak demand to reach 87.5 gigawatts — 2 gigawatts higher than the current record.

[ERCOT](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eND0tL88BVHcxBeP7dj5mAYIoWUhViIVawFybCcazduJIcm2OkMsR5M2xsQQFgMmg3BXC0iOQ1SO_x7bZuzG2EQqpyxrKV8983uMSm14arnBoIza9TIBmvaPWPd9W8pMoXESJdAkqAYsdfDZ58OZmnHEfwlJ-plxmvxpbrf3mpMYljsqzMK3xn3sxCoK-ppaZW7ClTg39sjflAZg9t4-n9Ufo96sirSG8rRuH4kYxiazdMem-RC0CWiq3YXU_3cCYagx2lwbVHgWvBvRRzqVvUNCeDyU265fmyMpABTjlH3-Nhm2HcY7gCbvRiaWI4awSKFfFMOx3F4nTK5ecdaB9xGYBKdg8H3Mp-6qQycNAo3l7wbvdHm8DhzyA5oW5Sk9zgDz6Hwn-_VStwJCgufiC8Z9udeyGuTaGheU2q7odSCj/4hn/NabMlHgBQi6S-R2Kzsv5IA/h21/h001.kLAavCAUtJlwZbs2BamUzsmIDZ5Hck1_hWYT-DxmQNQ) President and CEO **Pablo Vegas** said the grid he oversees is ready to handle it.

“The state of the grid is strong,” he told board members Tuesday. “It is as reliable as it has ever been, and it is as ready for the challenges of extreme weather that we have ever experienced. And so I feel confident that we are ready for this upcoming summer season.”

While ERCOT anticipates the state’s power plants will produce enough capacity to meet the demand, the state’s sagging transmission infrastructure could pose challenges moving that power to where it’s needed when it’s needed. A problematic circuit that makes a loop around San Antonio could cause cascading outages across the state if overloaded.

That’s why ERCOT is shelling out more than $110 million of its ratepayer-funded budget to tap a temporary generator fleet from Houston for about 450 megawatts and to keep an aging CPS Energy natural gas plant open past its prime — adding another 400 megawatts of power in the troubled area.

The old plant won’t be fixed up in time to operate this summer, but some of the generators will be ready to go in a couple weeks, Vegas announced.

It’s part of ERCOT’s plan to keep the lines from being overburdened, especially when plentiful power from South Texas wind farms and batteries is needed in North Texas, where generation capacity hasn’t kept up with increasing demand. The location of the plant, Unit 3 at Braunig Power Station, means that ERCOT can use it — along with the 15 generators, tied to nine key substations along the problematic circuit — to reduce the number of electrons zipping across the troubled power lines at times of high demand.

CPS already is working on a long-term fix for the transmission challenges — building out expanded power lines. At ERCOT’s request, they’ve speeded up the timeline to get the line upgrades completed.

The temporary generator fleet has a contentious past. It was originally under the control of Houston electricity and natural gas provider CenterPoint Energy as part of an $800 million contract with owner LifeCyle Power. It was intended to provide backup power to keep Houston powered amid severe weather.

But when Hurricane Beryl tore through Houston, knocking out power for days, most of the generators were never deployed. That’s because 15 of the 20 contracted machines take several days to assemble and need special permits — not well suited for sudden outages caused by a storm, despite being billed as “mobile generators” by CenterPoint.

Five of the generators already have been moved to San Antonio and four were fully assembled as of Tuesday. A second set of five were expected to arrive Wednesday.

“What the contract provides for is bringing roughly five generators online into the San Antonio area every 31 days, with the first generators beginning operation by the early part of July,” Vegas said.

Once they’re assembled, the generators can be fired up quickly to provide emergency backup services to support the transmission infrastructure while permanent line upgrades are ongoing.

The fleet is contracted until March 31, 2027, but can exit San Antonio sooner if the transmission expansion finishes up sooner. The contracted cost, to be shared by ratepayers across Texas, is $54 million." Sign up now and invite your friends and family to be part of the informed. | TOP NEWS “Former Ken Paxton aides allege witness tampering during impeachment trial, ” Austin American-Statesman's Taylor Goldenstein – “Several former and current top aides of Attorney General Ken Paxton are trading explosive accusations in legal and administrative filings, the latest of which alleges that Paxton's right-hand deputy obstructed justice and tampered with witnesses during his 2023 impeachment. The public feud could become a distraction for Paxton just as he’s overcome a series of legal troubles, including the impeachment charges, which he was , and as he launches his bid to unseat U.S. Sen. John Cornyn in next year’s Republican primary. The new allegations — detailed in a suit filed Wednesday in federal court in Austin by former Solicitor General Judd Stone andChris Hilton , the former chief of the general litigation division — include claims that current First Assistant Attorney General Brent Webster threatened to fire employees if they gave testimony during the impeachment proceedings that was unfavorable to Paxton. The claim has not previously been reported, and Webster did not immediately respond to a request for comment. » It’s not clear if the claims were ever raised to law enforcement; Webster has not been charged with any criminal wrongdoing. The first lawsuit was filed last month by Jordan Eskew , a former executive assistant for Stone and Hilton, against the two men and their private law firm. Eskew accused Stone of sexual harassment on multiple occasions in 2023 when she had taken leave from Paxton’s office to work for Stone and Hilton as private attorneys representing Paxton in the impeachment trial. She also claimed Hilton failed to protect her and that the two created a hostile work environment. » A spokesperson for Stone and Hilton’s law firm has called Eskew’s suit “a complete fabrication” and said that it was pushed by Paxton’s top deputy, Webster, who has a “personal vendetta” against Stone and Hilton. Webster and Eskew are still working at the attorney general’s office. This week, Stone and Hilton shot back with a suit of their own against Webster and other attorney general staffers, not including Eskew, and a bar complaint against Webster . They claim Webster tried to damage their careers by lying about them and encouraging Eskew to file her sexual harassment suit. Stone and Hilton also claimed in the filing to the State Bar of Texas that Webster tried to tamper with potential witnesses for Paxton’s impeachment proceedings by pressuring them to give favorable testimony or “to flee the state to evade being subpoenaed to disclose information harmful to Webster.” It does not specify which people were targeted. Webster also demanded that Stone and Hilton “disclose confidential information” during the impeachment proceedings, which would have violated their professional obligation to Paxton, according to the bar complaint. When they refused to share the information, the complaint alleges, Webster threatened retaliation against them and the firm. The bar complaint also alleges Webster abused the power of his office by, in part, leveraging meetings with private citizens and lawyers to try to obtain future lucrative employment and harm his enemies. The Bar’s law office will now review the complaint and decide within the next 30 days whether the allegations amount to professional misconduct, and if so, it will conduct an investigation. The harassment claims Eskew’s lawsuit claims Stone made a sexual comment and yelled at her several times at their law firm, and Hilton stood by and did nothing. She alleges that Stone responded to her statement at a work lunch that a shot of alcohol was “the most disgusting thing I have ever tasted” by saying, “I highly doubt that is the most disgusting thing that has ever been in your mouth.” Hilton, according to the complaint, did nothing but wince and laugh uncomfortably. It also described a situation in which Stone and Hilton berated Eskew for taking too long to get a BBQ lunch to the staff and multiple other occasions in which Stone yelled at her and other female employees. It alleged Stone called her “white trash” because she was wearing turquoise earrings and that he asked her to buy alcohol and make drinks as part of her job duties. One time, the suit alleges, Stone told her: “If anyone else makes a comment about my drinking, they’ll be fired.” Another time, he told her that at his firm, “you can say whatever slurs you want.” The Texas Workforce Commission previously determined that Eskew had grounds to bring a harassment suit, and in a filing to the TWC, Stone admitted to making the comments but “denied the sexual nature” of them, according to Eskew’s suit. Stone, Hilton and Eskew were among the lawyers who took leave from the attorney general’s office in 2023 to represent Paxton during the impeachment. Eskew claims that upon their return, they were asked to resign after she raised concerns about their behavior during the impeachment period. They deny that they were forced to leave, and their suit suggests they left because of their differences with Webster. Stone and Hilton declined an interview request for this story. Four other lawyers who returned to the attorney general’s office after working at Stone and Hilton’s private firm during the impeachment process have entered into paid settlement agreements that prohibit them from disparaging the firm owners, according to the suit, though it does not say when. They agreed to a statement saying the lawyers “parted ways professionally” and “amiably” with Stone and Hilton. Eskew refused to agree to the statement, according to the suit. The Webster connection Webster wasn’t a plaintiff in Eskew’s suit, but he indicated in an internal email cited in the complaint that two women who worked with Stone and Hilton told him they were afraid of potential assault or further harassment by the men. Webster also wrote that he had heard from one of the women that Stone had openly fantasized about Webster being harmed and as a result, Webster feared for his and his family’s safety. Stone and Hilton denied Webster’s account and all accusations of sexual harassment in Eskew’s filing. They claim Webster was angry with them for pushing to get access to records after they left that they believed would expose wrongdoing. “The email is nothing more than retaliation against Plaintiffs for their refusal to play ball with a corrupt public official,” their suit reads. “Webster sent the email in response to Plaintiffs’ efforts to obtain documents that would prove his corruption.” Eskew’s lawsuit has caused Stone and Hilton “significant embarrassment and a loss of standing in their professional and personal circles — just as Defendants intended,” they write in their suit. Days after Eskew’s suit went public, Stone stepped down from the Federal Judicial Evaluation Committee, a panel of attorneys who screen judicial candidates for Texas’ two senators, saying he did not want “the recent false and scurrilous accusations against me to overshadow the committee,” ." ($) “ERCOT hustling to prepare Texas electric grid for record summer demand, ” San Antonio Express-News' Sara DiNatale – “Bracing for record-high demand this summer, the Texas grid operator is setting up temporary generators at San Antonio substations as part of to prevent a statewide transmission meltdown. The said its latest forecast calls for this summer’s peak demand to reach 87.5 gigawatts — 2 gigawatts higher than the current record. President and CEO Pablo Vegas said the grid he oversees is ready to handle it. “The state of the grid is strong,” he told board members Tuesday. “It is as reliable as it has ever been, and it is as ready for the challenges of extreme weather that we have ever experienced. And so I feel confident that we are ready for this upcoming summer season.” While ERCOT anticipates the state’s power plants will produce enough capacity to meet the demand, the state’s sagging transmission infrastructure could pose challenges moving that power to where it’s needed when it’s needed. A problematic circuit that makes a loop around San Antonio could cause cascading outages across the state if overloaded. That’s why ERCOT is shelling out more than $110 million of its ratepayer-funded budget to tap a temporary generator fleet from Houston for about 450 megawatts and to keep an aging CPS Energy natural gas plant open past its prime — adding another 400 megawatts of power in the troubled area. The old plant won’t be fixed up in time to operate this summer, but some of the generators will be ready to go in a couple weeks, Vegas announced. It’s part of ERCOT’s plan to keep the lines from being overburdened, especially when plentiful power from South Texas wind farms and batteries is needed in North Texas, where generation capacity hasn’t kept up with increasing demand. The location of the plant, Unit 3 at Braunig Power Station, means that ERCOT can use it — along with the 15 generators, tied to nine key substations along the problematic circuit — to reduce the number of electrons zipping across the troubled power lines at times of high demand. CPS already is working on a long-term fix for the transmission challenges — building out expanded power lines. At ERCOT’s request, they’ve speeded up the timeline to get the line upgrades completed. The temporary generator fleet has a contentious past. It was originally under the control of Houston electricity and natural gas provider CenterPoint Energy as part of an $800 million contract with owner LifeCyle Power. It was intended to provide backup power to keep Houston powered amid severe weather. But when Hurricane Beryl tore through Houston, knocking out power for days, most of the generators were never deployed. That’s because 15 of the 20 contracted machines take several days to assemble and need special permits — not well suited for sudden outages caused by a storm, despite being billed as “mobile generators” by CenterPoint. Five of the generators already have been moved to San Antonio and four were fully assembled as of Tuesday. A second set of five were expected to arrive Wednesday. “What the contract provides for is bringing roughly five generators online into the San Antonio area every 31 days, with the first generators beginning operation by the early part of July,” Vegas said. Once they’re assembled, the generators can be fired up quickly to provide emergency backup services to support the transmission infrastructure while permanent line upgrades are ongoing. The fleet is contracted until March 31, 2027, but can exit San Antonio sooner if the transmission expansion finishes up sooner. clean_body: To view this mail in a browser, copy into your browser. TELL SENATORS: SAY NO TO SELL-OFFS Senators are negotiating a bill that would sell off public lands to billionaire polluters. We can’t afford to let them put our future at risk — tell your senators to oppose ANY attempt to gut incentives for clean energy or roll back protections for our air, lands, and water. TAKE ACTION Peter, Senate Republicans are continuing to push provisions in their big, ugly bill to sell off public lands while continuing to dramatically cut clean energy. The legislation would require selling off America’s public lands to Big Polluters and allowing them to drill in some of the last wild places like the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. Time is running out. The Senate could vote on this disastrous public lands sell-off as soon as this week.We need to act now before the bill makes its way through the Senate and the final vote happens. People across the country are making their voices heard. We can’t afford to sell out our public lands, our economy, and our future to polluters — tell your senators to oppose ANY attempt to gut incentives for clean energy or roll back protections for our air, lands, and water. The Republican majority in the Senate is razor-thin, and a number of Republican senators have already spoken out against a sledgehammer approach to our public lands and clean energy investments. Without their votes, the bill cannot pass into law, but there’s enormous pressure on them to cave to Trump. We need to show the Senate how unpopular selling off public lands and gutting clean energy is, and it will take ALL of us. The best thing you can do for the environment right now is to tell your senators to protect our public lands and clean energy incentives in the final bill. Thank you for being with us, Peter. | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253484/553751233/-577349673?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_250625_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZjJjODZmMC0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ztxcXQhN6pCG_c71PLFgWOfUnntMR9_ihAwTbb-qyhw=) Derek,

I know I’ve been sending you a lot of emails about my reelection race in Virginia these days, but today, I want to take a step back and reintroduce myself.

[_**But first, please consider chipping in to my reelection campaign before my end-of-quarter deadline to protect my seat and take back the Senate for Democrats.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253485/553751234/-577349673?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_250625_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZjJjODZmMC0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ztxcXQhN6pCG_c71PLFgWOfUnntMR9_ihAwTbb-qyhw=)

Like so many Americans, I grew up in a middle-class family and was lucky enough to attend good public schools. I have a vivid memory of being the Richard Nixon surrogate in my 8th grade class – yes I know, I’ve come a long way. I have my 8th grade history teacher, Jim Tyler, to thank for setting me on the path to being a Democrat. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253486/553751235/-577349673?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_250625_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZjJjODZmMC0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ztxcXQhN6pCG_c71PLFgWOfUnntMR9_ihAwTbb-qyhw=) Fast forward a few years, I became the first person in my family to graduate from college, made possible by working multiple jobs and taking out student loans. That’s something I’m incredibly proud of.

Before I became a U.S. Senator, I actually started out in business. I invested my entire life savings, a few thousand dollars, into my first venture... which failed in about 6 weeks, by the way. My second venture did a little better, lasting six months, but it wasn’t until my third try that things started to look up. I’m extremely proud to have founded what became one of Virginia’s leading tech companies.

It was actually that experience that got me into public service. I thought that everybody in this country ought to have the same kind of fair shot that I had. So, I ran for governor in Virginia, and won. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253487/553751236/-577349673?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_250625_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZjJjODZmMC0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ztxcXQhN6pCG_c71PLFgWOfUnntMR9_ihAwTbb-qyhw=) And if you can believe it, my good friend Tim Kaine (now my fellow Virginia senator) was my Lieutenant Governor. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253488/553751237/-577349673?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_250625_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZjJjODZmMC0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ztxcXQhN6pCG_c71PLFgWOfUnntMR9_ihAwTbb-qyhw=) After our four years in the governor’s office, Virginia was rated the best state for business, the best managed state, _and_ the best state to receive a public education. But even then, I knew that my work to make sure that _every_ family – no matter their background – has the same shot that I did, was far from over.

That’s when I ran for the United States Senate, and won. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253489/553751238/-577349673?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_250625_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZjJjODZmMC0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ztxcXQhN6pCG_c71PLFgWOfUnntMR9_ihAwTbb-qyhw=) In the Senate, I helped spearhead the largest infrastructure and public lands investments in half a century, worked to significantly expand Virginia’s domestic manufacturing, and have fought to lower health care costs across the Commonwealth. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253490/553751239/-577349673?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_250625_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZjJjODZmMC0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ztxcXQhN6pCG_c71PLFgWOfUnntMR9_ihAwTbb-qyhw=) **But I have to tell you, in my time in the Senate – maybe in my time in politics – there has been nothing as challenging, as bizarre, and as _holy sugar_ as the last 157 days of the second Trump administration.**

This administration's corruption has made every American less safe. Trump is implementing tariffs causing prices to skyrocket for working families, refusing to fire Pete Hegseth even after he shared classified information on an unsecured platform, and backing the largest cuts to Medicaid in history to fund big tax giveaways for the wealthiest Americans.

I didn’t get into politics to let people like Trump and Elon dismantle our federal government and rebuild it for billionaires like themselves. I’m proud to lead the fight against their corrupt administration, but I can’t do it alone.

[_**So I’m asking: can I count on you to pitch in today to protect my seat in the Senate so I can keep up my work to hold this administration accountable and continue delivering for Virginia’s communities? The road ahead will not be easy, but I know if we all stand up and speak out, we will fight back and win.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253491/553751240/-577349673?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_250625_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZjJjODZmMC0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ztxcXQhN6pCG_c71PLFgWOfUnntMR9_ihAwTbb-qyhw=) body:
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253470/553751215/-1591572682?refcode=250625_MFC_Annie_22YearsOfNothing&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmOTU5ZmUzNi0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=T68fFd1AfJ8h7wOekx9SrvCdmzH0IzwJCZzAKdsPpy0=) Friend, I’m Dr. Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, a mom of three, and the Democrat running for U.S. Senate to defeat Republican Lindsey Graham in South Carolina. If we flip this seat, we can end Lindsey Graham’s career and help Democrats retake the Senate, and expand the map for Democrats in future elections I know this won’t be easy. But I’ve treated kids who were shot, hospitalized, and failed by broken systems. Nothing about this moment feels optional. [**We need an overwhelming surge of grassroots support in these early days to prove that we can finally defeat Lindsey Graham. So I’m humbly asking: Will you chip in a split donation of $50, $25, or even a $3 donation between Seth Moulton and my campaign before midnight to become a Founding Donor of my campaign? >>**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253471/553751216/1094341437?refcode=250625_MFC_Annie_22YearsOfNothing&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmOTU5ZmUzNi0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=T68fFd1AfJ8h7wOekx9SrvCdmzH0IzwJCZzAKdsPpy0=) Let me introduce myself. I’ve spent nearly 20 years serving my community as a pediatrician, treating everything from asthma and violent trauma to the emotional toll of growing up in poverty. I’ve seen what bad policy does to good families — and I’ve seen kids suffer because people like Lindsey Graham would rather protect their own power than protect children. In 2022, after 15 years of working in hospitals, I ran for Congress because I knew our kids needed a voice in Washington. I lost — and I told my oldest daughter I wouldn’t run again. But then Trump’s chaos came back. And Lindsey Graham? He cheered. The truth is, I’m scared. And I’m angry. And I’m done waiting. So I’m stepping up — because our kids, and this country can’t afford another six years of Lindsey Graham. I’m building a people-powered campaign to flip South Carolina and give kids the voice they deserve. And I need your help. [Donate](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253472/553751217/-1591572682?refcode=250625_MFC_Annie_22YearsOfNothing&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmOTU5ZmUzNi0xMzUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=T68fFd1AfJ8h7wOekx9SrvCdmzH0IzwJCZzAKdsPpy0=) Thank you — from the bottom of my heart. This campaign is for the kids, but it only works with you in it. Until the kids are alright, Dr. Annie Andrews
Democratic Candidate for U.S. Senate

I’m building a people-powered campaign to flip South Carolina and give kids the voice they deserve. And I need your help. = Thank you — from the bottom of my heart. clean_body: The MAGA Supreme Court just told Trump he could go ahead and send immigrants to countries they have no connection to. . | | Peter, Yesterday, the MAGA Supreme Court dropped a one-paragraph order giving Trump the green light to deport immigrants to countries they’ve never been to before. Previously, lower court judges had stepped in to protect due process and block the Trump administration from sending migrants to South Sudan.But the bought-and-paid for corrupt Supreme Court stepped in to enable Trump’s oppressive agenda and further erode the rule of law. The decision allows the Trump administration to round up any immigrants they feel like and send them straight to a country like El Salvador or South Sudan without the chance to challenge their deportation before a judge. And they did it all with zero explanation, anonymously issuing their ruling through the “shadow docket” after hearing no oral arguments and without full briefings. The Trump administration has been flooding the Court with such requests, knowing the MAGA justices will quietly bless their worst impulses. It’s bad enough that Trump is now allowed to deport people to countries they’ve never set foot in with less than 16 hours of notice and no court hearing. The decision also allows him to send immigrants to countries in which they face increased threats of violence and torture. It’s yet another example of the MAGA justices on the Supreme Court rubber stamping Donald Trump’s horrific and chaotic immigration policies. We can’t sit by while the Roberts Court ignores and even rewards the administration’s blatant disregard for the law. The fact that the Trump administration was able to win this argument even after violating the lower court’s ruling is despicable—and extraordinarily telling. The extremist, billionaire forces behind the MAGA Court are getting exactly what they paid for. But our judicial system doesn’t work for them—it works for us. body:
Patriot ,

My name is Scott Brown, and I want to take a few minutes to share my story
with you and how the experiences and lessons I’ve learned have led me to make a
big decision this week.
I had a challenging upbringing. My mom was married and divorced four times,
and my dad was married and divorced three times. I was raised by my single mom,
who worked multiple jobs to put food on the table. We didn’t have much, but
with the love and support of my grandparents, we had a fighting chance. We
moved often—I lived in 17 different places before I turned 18.

<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaea_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
I know what it’s like to worry about where your next meal is coming from or
whether the bills all get paid.And those early years taught me the value of
grit, of resilience, and hard work.

Nothing in my life has ever been handed to me — I’ve had to fight for every
step forward.

I worked my way through college and law school, taking any odd job and doing
whatever it took to stay afloat.

At 19, I joined the Army National Guard. I served for more than 30 years and
retired as a Colonel. I’ve worn our nation’s uniform with pride and know
firsthand what it means to serve a cause bigger than yourself.

<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaea_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
Back in 2010, I took a leap that many thought was crazy. I ran for the U.S.
Senate in Massachusetts as a Republican,driven by a belief that people like you
deserved a real voice in Washington, not just another career politician. I
drove across the state, putting countless miles on my beloved truck, a 2005 GMC
Canyon. With the incredible support of grassroots supporters like you from all
corners of the country,we pulled off a stunning upset and won, shaking the
political establishment to its core.

But that victory was just the start.

I went to Washington as a disruptor, refusing to play the insider games of
career politicians. That made me a target. The national Democrats zeroed in,
recruiting Elizabeth Warren and pouring tens of millions into a campaign to
defeat me. Despite our best efforts, we came up short in that race.

But I wasn’t discouraged. I believed then, and I believe now, that there’s a
bigger plan for all of us.

My wife, Gail, and I became four-time grandparents, and we’ve poured our
hearts into our family and our New Hampshire community. In 2017, when President
Trump asked me to serve as U.S. Ambassador to New Zealand and Samoa,I was
honored to represent our nation, strengthen global partnerships, and protect
American interests abroad.
<https://secure.winred.com/nrsc/doge-hit-ground-running-tc-rs-hf/?recurring=true&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&address=&zip=&city=&state=&employer_name=&occupation=&amtposition=4>

<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaea_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
Today, I’m writing to you with big news: I’m not done fighting. Our country’s
future is at a crossroads, and I’m stepping up again to run for the U.S. Senate
in New Hampshire.I’m doing this for you, for our shared values, and for the
America we believe in. Chip in to Join Scott Brown »
<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaea_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
You’ve seen what happens when Democrats hold unchecked power...

Runaway inflation...

Chaos at our southern border...

Soft-on-crime policies...

Men in women’s sports and locker rooms...

Foreign policy missteps that weaken our allies and embolden our enemies.

Hardworking Americans like you are being left behind, and we can’t let this
radical agenda take over the Senate in 2026.The stakes are just too high.

Here’s the truth: I can’t do this without you.

The Democrats and their elite allies will flood this race with MILLIONS. It’s
an open seat in a swing state. They don’t want someone like me—someone who
speaks plainly, serves with honor, and refuses to sell out—anywhere near
Washington.

That’s why I’m reaching out to you today, asking you to stand with me from
Day One.

A contribution of $5, $10, or whatever you can give will help us build a
campaign powered by people like you, not political insiders.
<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaea_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
Every dollar counts, and every voice matters. Chip in to Join Scott Brown »
<https://secure.winred.com/scott-brown-for-new-hampshire-inc/bio-brown-hf-launch-acs/?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_aaea_acs&utm_campaign=20250625_bio-launch_sb>
If you’ve ever felt like your voice doesn’t matter, I’m here to tell you it
does. It matters to me. And it’s the only reason I’m in this fight.

Let’s do this together.

Scott Brown
Candidate for U.S. Senate

| | This past weekend, I was holding town halls in Eastern Oregon. In Malheur County – which has the highest percentage of Medicaid recipients of any Oregon county, and one of the highest in the country – I held a roundtable to listen to and to uplift the stories of Oregonians that are terrified of the Republicans' looming Medicaid cuts. I even invited the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator, Dr. Mehmet Oz, to join me. During his confirmation hearing, he promised to join me in Malheur County to answer directly to Oregonians about why the Trump administration is pursuing such dangerous and deadly cuts to health care. **He was a no-show.** The Trump administration is hiding from the American people because they know there is no real excuse for kicking 16 million people off their health care. The stakes got even higher recently when Senate Republicans made changes to the bill to make **_even deeper_****cuts to Medicaid, which will result in millions more being kicked off their health care, and would force hospitals and nursing homes to shutter.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110253689/553751902/-2044921950?refcode=2025-06-25-medicaid&recurring=0&amount=4&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=37ddb206-1652-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzN2RkYjIwNi0xNjUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5PKBoF_pFLIH-wE7wDWRTb9k7UFL8npzMkRBrnXm8v4=) On behalf of Oregonians – and all Americans – who depend on Medicaid to make visits to the doctor's office and get life-saving care, **I'm going to do all I can to fight these cuts.** I'm going to amplify the voices of those who have everything on the line. I'm going to take our message to all corners of media, and ramp up pressure on waffling Republicans in both the House and Senate who fear the political fallout if they cut their constituents' care. # **The US Senate is Getting Ready to Vote for the Biggest Cut to Healthcare in American History**
_**The Republican Big, BAD Bill includes huge cuts to healthcare, food assistance, and student loan support ...and a big tax handout for the wealthiest in our country.**_ [](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100170218.172852.596&gen=1&mailing_linkid=14851) [It's been reported that the US Senate will vote on Friday for what Republicans are calling the "Big, Beautiful Bill"](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100170218.172852.596&gen=1&mailing_linkid=14852). If it passes the Senate, the bill will make massive cuts to healthcare, food assistance, student loan support, good paying jobs, and a lot more. Everything about this bill is BAD, including that the cuts are being used to provide the richest in our country a huge tax giveaway.
* * *

name: Amanda Zurawski
subject: Three years after Roe
body:
This crisis is political — and we can fix it at the ballot box. |
---
[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110255543/553757884/-1686146655?refcode=WUEFE662_20250625_Zurawski_PL_v1s3&sourceid=1056444&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ZmYzYzQ2Ny0xZTUyLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6viTU_hNL2vepnKraAYLl2RnBl-EeUSWEKskkO1Peis=) Peter,

My name is Amanda Zurawski. And I nearly died because of an abortion ban.

When my water broke at 18 weeks, there was no chance the baby I so deeply wanted would survive. But because a fetal heartbeat was still present, the abortion bans in Texas prohibited my doctors from intervening until my own life was in danger. I ended up in septic shock. I spent days in the ICU. And it was terrifying.

That trauma was preventable. But in a post-_Roe_ America, it's become heartbreakingly common. And not everyone has survived.

Yesterday marked three years since the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_. And I've spent nearly every day since fighting to make sure no one else has to go through what I did.

I've filed a lawsuit. Traveled with Vice President Kamala Harris. Helped take a documentary about my experience across the country. Told my story on the national stage. And through it all, one thing has become painfully clear:

**This crisis is political — and fixing it starts at the ballot box.**

That's why I'm proud to stand with EMILYs List. They're working to elect Democratic pro-choice women across the country — women who will fight for our rights and refuse to let extremist Republicans dictate our medical care. ****[**If you're as outraged as I am, I hope you'll donate now. We can't undo what's happened, but we can make damn sure it never happens again — by helping EMILYs List women take back power nationwide. clean_body: This crisis is political — and we can fix it at the ballot box. | = Peter, My name is Amanda Zurawski. And I nearly died because of an abortion ban. When my water broke at 18 weeks, there was no chance the baby I so deeply wanted would survive. But because a fetal heartbeat was still present, the abortion bans in Texas prohibited my doctors from intervening until my own life was in danger. I ended up in septic shock. I spent days in the ICU. And it was terrifying. That trauma was preventable. But in a post-Roe America, it's become heartbreakingly common. And not everyone has survived. Yesterday marked three years since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade. And I've spent nearly every day since fighting to make sure no one else has to go through what I did. I've filed a lawsuit. Traveled with Vice President Kamala Harris. Helped take a documentary about my experience across the country. Told my story on the national stage. And through it all, one thing has become painfully clear: This crisis is political — and fixing it starts at the ballot box. That's why I'm proud to stand with EMILYs List. They're working to elect Democratic pro-choice women across the country — women who will fight for our rights and refuse to let extremist Republicans dictate our medical care. **=** If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = With hope, Amanda = | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Thank you for being a supporter of EMILYs List. name: Deb Haaland
subject: Quickly join me in OPPOSING Republican efforts to sell off our public lands
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO
body:
Every American who cares about protecting the outdoors has reason to be angry right now.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=2838%2E400544%2EsGQiro)
If you care about the outdoors, I need you to join me in taking urgent action today.
**Republicans in the Senate recently unveiled a new plan to auction off millions of acres of public land to private developers.**
Every American who cares about our country’s natural landscapes has reason to be angry at this plan. If this addition to their so-called “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” gets signed into law, this move could represent the single largest sale of national public lands in modern history – _all to pay for tax cuts for the richest people in the country._
And although the Senate parliamentarian ruled that the original plan could not go forward under the reconciliation process, the author has vowed to revise the plan to make it compatible with Senate rules.
There’s still time to stop this. But only if enough of us speak out against this unjust and irresponsible sale of our beloved public lands.
[**Quickly add your name to join me in OPPOSING the sale of our public lands. We all must speak up to tell Senate Republicans that our access to the outdoors is not for sale.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_ms_DH_20250625_2_publiclands?source=em20250625-2838&akid=2838%2E400544%2EsGQiro)
**[Add Your Name »](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_ms_DH_20250625_2_publiclands?source=em20250625-2838&akid=2838%2E400544%2EsGQiro)**
This has been Trump’s playbook all along. He’s defunding the agencies who steward our public lands in order to auction them off to the highest bidder – with zero regard for the grave and irreversible consequences.
Now, if Republican Senators get their way, our local recreation areas, wilderness study areas, critical wildlife habitats, and big game migration corridors across the American West will all be eligible for sale to private interests – all to offset the cost of huge tax breaks for multi-millionaires and billionaires.

The memories I made fishing, camping, and hiking on our public lands when I was a young girl are what inspired my lifelong dedication to protecting the outdoors, and it breaks my heart to imagine those same opportunities being stolen from our children and grandchildren. That’s why I am personally asking you to sign on today:
[**Sign on to OPPOSE this forced sale of millions of acres of American public land. To stop this from passing, we must gather as many signatures as possible to tell Senate Republicans that our public lands are not for sale.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_ms_DH_20250625_2_publiclands?source=em20250625-2838&akid=2838%2E400544%2EsGQiro)
**[Add Your Name »](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_ms_DH_20250625_2_publiclands?source=em20250625-2838&akid=2838%2E400544%2EsGQiro)**
Our public lands belong to all of us. Thank you for standing up for the lands and future our children will inherit.
—Deb
P.S. As Secretary of the Interior, I helped protect millions of acres of public land across our country. But now, all of the progress we fought for is on the chopping block. [**Please take just one minute to add your name to my urgent petition to OPPOSE this massive sale of America’s public lands.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_ms_DH_20250625_2_publiclands?source=em20250625-2838&akid=2838%2E400544%2EsGQiro)

Republicans in the Senate recently unveiled a new plan to auction off millions of acres of public land to private developers. Every American who cares about our country’s natural landscapes has reason to be angry at this plan. If this addition to their so-called “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” gets signed into law, this move could represent the single largest sale of national public lands in modern history – all to pay for tax cuts for the richest people in the country. And although the Senate parliamentarian ruled that the original plan could not go forward under the reconciliation process, the author has vowed to revise the plan to make it compatible with Senate rules. There’s still time to stop this. But only if enough of us speak out against this unjust and irresponsible sale of our beloved public lands. This has been Trump’s playbook all along. He’s defunding the agencies who steward our public lands in order to auction them off to the highest bidder – with zero regard for the grave and irreversible consequences. Now, if Republican Senators get their way, our local recreation areas, wilderness study areas, critical wildlife habitats, and big game migration corridors across the American West will all be eligible for sale to private interests – all to offset the cost of huge tax breaks for multi-millionaires and billionaires. The memories I made fishing, camping, and hiking on our public lands when I was a young girl are what inspired my lifelong dedication to protecting the outdoors, and it breaks my heart to imagine those same opportunities being stolen from our children and grandchildren. That’s why I am personally asking you to sign on today: Our public lands belong to all of us. Thank you for standing up for the lands and future our children will inherit. —Deb P.S. As Secretary of the Interior, I helped protect millions of acres of public land across our country. But now, all of the progress we fought for is on the chopping block.
